lessons.lesson_title: Freelance Operations, Proposals, Value Pricing & Client Revisions
lessons.what_is_taught: The commercial client lifecycle: discovery calls, authoring scopes of work, value-based pricing vs flat project rates vs hourly rates, milestone billing, contract agreements. Revision governance: structuring contracts with 2 included revision rounds, change order fees, diplomatically decoding subjective client feedback, and approval sign-offs.
subtopics: The end-to-end client lifecycle: Discovery, Proposal, Contract/Deposit, Brief, Milestones, Revisions, Final Delivery
Pricing strategies for graphic designers: calculating hourly rates, flat project packages, and value-based commercial pricing
Authoring commercial proposals and scopes of work: defining deliverables, timelines, payment terms, and out-of-scope clauses
Revision governance: structuring contracts with 2 included revision rounds and handling scope creep professionally
Managing client feedback: translating subjective remarks ('make it pop', 'make it look more corporate') into concrete visual solutions
Client approval workflows: milestone sign-off sheets and protecting your intellectual property before final payment
lessons.why_it_matters: Talented designers frequently fail in freelance or agency careers because of poor business operations: underpricing their work, tolerating endless scope creep, or reacting emotionally to client criticism. Professional business operations guarantee profitability and client respect.
lessons.what_learner_does: Author a commercial project proposal and scope-of-work contract for a client rebrand project; calculate value pricing; draft a professional written response to 3 challenging client revision requests.
lessons.expected_outcome: A completed commercial Freelance Proposal & Scope-of-Work Contract template and a client communication response sheet.
lessons.example: Professionally responding to a client requesting to 'make the logo 3x bigger' by explaining how an oversized mark impairs visual hierarchy and reduces conversion focus on the call-to-action button.

lessons.lesson_title: Portfolio Curation, Case Study Architecture & Behance Presentation
lessons.what_is_taught: The psychology of design recruiters and agency creative directors: reviewing 50 portfolios in 30 minutes. Case study structure: The Problem, The Brand Strategy, Design Process (sketches, moodboards), The Solution, Deliverables in Context, The Result. Designing cohesive 1400px wide Behance case study presentation slides.
subtopics: Portfolio curation: selecting 4 strong, diverse case studies over 20 mediocre pieces ('you are judged by your weakest project')
The 6-stage case study narrative: Client Problem, Strategic Brief, Process Artifacts, The Solution, Collateral in Context, Results
Designing 1400px wide Behance presentation slides in Photoshop/Illustrator with cohesive typography and spacing
Mockup presentation ethics: using high-end, realistic 3D mockups without letting the mockup overpower the design artwork
Authoring compelling case study copy: explaining *why* design decisions were made, font pairings chosen, and color palettes selected
Publishing on Behance and exporting an executive PDF portfolio presentation deck for offline interviews
lessons.why_it_matters: A portfolio of flat, disconnected JPEGs gets immediately passed over by recruiters. Agencies hire graphic designers who prove their problem-solving ability, strategic thinking, and non-destructive execution through structured case studies.
lessons.what_learner_does: Design an 8-slide Behance case study presentation for one of your course projects, showcasing sketches, color formulas, typography scales, vector wireframes, and 3D mockups in context.
lessons.expected_outcome: A published or presentation-ready Behance case study URL or high-resolution PDF portfolio presentation deck.
lessons.example: Opening a case study with a bold 3D hero mockup of the packaging in a retail setting, followed by the client brief, competitor research, 20 thumbnail sketches, and final vector guidelines.

lessons.lesson_title: 1-Page ATS Designer Resume, Personal Branding & Interview Defense
lessons.what_is_taught: Typesetting an ATS-compliant 1-page designer resume in Adobe InDesign: typographic hierarchy, margin constraints, avoiding graphic progress bars. Establishing personal branding: personal monogram, cohesive LinkedIn and Behance header banners. Preparing for 10-minute verbal portfolio interview defenses and live design tests.
subtopics: Why over-designed resumes with rating bars (e.g. 'Photoshop 85%') get rejected by applicant tracking systems and agency HR
Typesetting a clean 1-page ATS-friendly resume in InDesign: single-column layout, clear hierarchy, standard headings
Personal brand identity: developing a personal designer monogram, personal color palette, and email signature
The 10-minute portfolio interview defense: structuring the verbal walkthrough of your top 2 case studies
Handling live agency design tests: time management, reading instructions, non-destructive file hygiene under pressure
Salary negotiation benchmarks for junior graphic design roles in India (₹2.2–₹3.8 LPA)
lessons.why_it_matters: A designer's resume is their first typography test. An unaligned or over-decorated resume signals poor typographic discipline before the recruiter even opens the portfolio. A confident verbal defense wins job offers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Typeset an ATS-compliant 1-page resume in InDesign; design personal brand banners; participate in a simulated 10-minute portfolio interview defense walkthrough.
lessons.expected_outcome: A print-ready and digital 1-page Designer Resume PDF, personal brand identity assets, and recorded portfolio defense walkthrough.
lessons.example: Articulating during an agency interview why an 8pt baseline grid and a humanist sans-serif typeface were selected to maximize legibility on a healthcare brand mobile ad campaign.

lessons.lesson_title: Final Capstone Integration, Forensic Production Audit & Defense
lessons.what_is_taught: Integration and finishing of the comprehensive Commercial Brand Launch Capstone. Forensic preflight audit of all capstone source files: verifying closed vector paths, expanding strokes, checking 300 DPI effective resolution on links, auditing color spaces, organizing client handover archives, and final graduation review.
subtopics: Integrating prior module outputs into the unified Commercial Brand Launch Capstone package
Forensic vector audit: checking all Illustrator artboards in Outline mode (`Ctrl+Y`) for stray points and unexpanded strokes
Forensic Photoshop audit: verifying layer masks, Smart Object linkages, and color profiles (sRGB for web, CMYK for print)
Forensic InDesign audit: running Live Preflight on the Brand Guidelines manual with zero errors and certified PDF/X-4 export
Structuring the client handover archive: master folders, read-me instructions, and font licensing disclosures
Final independent portfolio defense panel: presenting the finished capstone and 4 modular case studies to instructors and peers
lessons.why_it_matters: Senior art directors and agency creative leads audit the candidate's actual source files. Messy, unorganized layers, unexpanded strokes, or missing font links instantly eliminate candidates from consideration.
lessons.what_learner_does: Perform peer and instructor preflight audits on all capstone source files; resolve all flagged QA issues; assemble the final graduation portfolio package; and present the capstone in a live defense.
lessons.expected_outcome: A certified, production-verified Capstone Project deliverable archive and completed 4-project graduation portfolio.
lessons.example: Packaging an InDesign document, ensuring zero overset text, 300 DPI effective resolution on all links, and expanded vector paths across all master brand assets.

modules.hands_on_practice: Assemble a commercial client proposal and contract, typeset a 1-page ATS designer resume in InDesign, author an 8-slide Behance case study presentation, perform a forensic preflight QA audit on all project source files, and defend the final Capstone Project in a live review panel.
modules.assignment: Deliver the Final Comprehensive Commercial Brand Launch Capstone: Brand Strategy Brief, Responsive Vector Logo Family (.AI, .EPS, .SVG, .PNG), 12-Page Brand Style Guide (.PDF), AI-Harmonized Key Visual Poster (.PSD), Omni-Channel Social Ad Kit (5 assets), Print-Ready Packaging Dieline & Collateral, and a published 1400px wide Behance Case Study Presentation.
modules.business_application: Empowers graduates to transition immediately into commercial graphic design employment, agency internships, or high-value freelance client operations with a verified, production-audited portfolio that commands respect.
modules.expected_outcome: A certified professional graduation portfolio consisting of 4 distinct commercial case studies plus the comprehensive final capstone project, packaged with clean source files, Behance presentation URLs, and an ATS-ready resume.

Design branching user flows and task flows mapping happy paths alongside error handling, empty states, and recovery paths.
Produce high-fidelity Figma visual interfaces adhering to the 8pt spatial grid system and modular typographic scales.
Build Auto Layout-based responsive designs utilizing nested frames, fluid constraints (Hug/Fill/Fixed), and min/max dimensions.

Design accessible digital interfaces strictly enforcing international WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, touch target, and focus requirements.

Conduct unmoderated and moderated usability tests in Maze, analyzing misclick heatmaps and calculating System Usability Scale (SUS) benchmarks.
Build and QA a fully responsive multi-page website in Framer across Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile viewport breakpoints.
Implement dynamic Framer CMS collections, dynamic detail page templates, and functional contact forms with validation states.
Apply purposeful motion and micro-interactions, configuring scroll transforms, scroll-triggered entrance reveals, and hover states.
Use Generative AI (Figma AI, Framer Agents, ChatGPT, Claude) responsibly in research and design while maintaining strict human authorship.
Document and present agency-grade professional case studies detailing problem framing, evidence, iterations, and business outcomes.
Prepare developer/client handoff packages utilizing Figma Dev Mode code inspection, technical annotations, and design tokens.

faq.question: Can I enroll in UI/UX Design Professional as a complete beginner with no prior design experience?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum begins from foundational principles. Module 01 introduces human-centered design thinking, user discovery, and problem framing before touching software. No prior design degree, coding background, or drawing talent is required.

faq.question: Is computer programming or coding required for this course?
faq.answer: No. This is a design and visual web engineering program. Instead of writing raw HTML, CSS, or JavaScript syntax, you learn web layout principles visually in Framer (Stacks, Grids, Breakpoints) and master developer collaboration using Figma Dev Mode.

faq.question: Is Figma taught from the absolute basics?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 begins with canvas navigation, frames, sections, vector networks, boolean operations, and 24x24px icon craftsmanship, systematically progressing into Auto Layout v5, Component Properties, and Figma Variables in Modules 04 and 05.

faq.question: Does the course cover actual user experience (UX) research?
faq.answer: Yes. UX research is heavily emphasized in Modules 01 and 02. You learn qualitative interview protocols, Google Forms screening surveys, FigJam affinity mapping, empathy mapping, validated user personas, customer journey maps, card sorting, and user flow diagramming.

faq.question: Does the curriculum cover advanced Auto Layout and Figma Variables?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 04 is dedicated to Auto Layout v5 (Direction, Wrap, Hug/Fill/Fixed sizing, min/max dimensions, absolute positioning) and Module 05 teaches multi-tier Figma Variables (Color, Spacing, Radius, String) with instant Light and Dark mode switching.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive multi-device design?
faq.answer: Yes. You learn responsive breakpoint architecture across Desktop (1200px+), Tablet (768px/810px), and Mobile (390px) viewports in both Figma (breakpoint component variants) and Framer (native responsive media queries).

faq.question: Can students create advanced interactive prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 06 teaches high-fidelity Figma prototyping using Smart Animate physics, custom Bézier easing curves, modal overlays, sticky navbars, nested horizontal carousels, and variable-driven conditional logic (If/Else) for interactive cart and form simulation.

faq.question: Will students learn Framer in this program?
faq.answer: Yes. Framer is a core primary software platform in this course, covered extensively across 28 guided instructional hours in Module 07, plus integration in Modules 08, 09, and 10.

faq.question: Will students create and launch an actual live Framer website?
faq.answer: Yes. In Module 07 and Case Study 03, every student builds and publishes a real, production-ready, 3-page responsive marketing website deployed to a live publicly accessible `.framer.media` domain.

faq.question: Does Framer hosting require a separate paid subscription?
faq.answer: No. Framer's free plan includes full visual canvas access, 3 responsive breakpoints, CMS collections up to 10 items, and free live hosting on `.framer.media` subdomains. All required coursework runs on the free tier; paid custom domain plans are completely optional.

faq.question: Are custom domains included in the course tuition fee?
faq.answer: No. Tuition covers full instructional training and hosting on free `.framer.media` subdomains. If you choose to connect a custom top-level domain (e.g. `yourname.com`), domain registration (~$12/year) and Framer's custom domain hosting plan are paid directly to those respective vendors.

faq.question: Is Framer CMS covered in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 07 covers Framer CMS collection schema modeling, binding dynamic fields (rich text, images, categories, dates) to canvas layers, designing dynamic collection detail page templates, and implementing category filtering.

faq.question: Does the course teach mobile hamburger navigation in Framer?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 07 features a mandatory responsive header lab where students construct a navigation component that displays horizontal links on desktop and automatically switches to an animated mobile hamburger drawer when the browser viewport resizes.

faq.question: Does the program cover Generative AI for UX research?
faq.answer: Yes. Modules 01 and 08 teach structured prompt engineering in ChatGPT and Claude for interview discussion guide scaffolding, qualitative transcript summarization, and microcopy ideation under strict human oversight (zero fabricated research allowed).

faq.question: Does the course teach Figma AI and Figma Make?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 08 covers Figma AI features (layer auto-renaming, visual asset search, wireframe scaffolding). Figma Make component prototyping is explored, accompanied by mandatory manual component prototyping fallbacks so no student is blocked by plan tier restrictions.

faq.question: Is Framer AI and Framer Agents included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 08 teaches the 2026 Framer Agents workflow for rapid page section scaffolding, responsive layout translation, and CMS drafting, followed by manual component refactoring to ensure accessible web standards.

faq.question: What is covered regarding the Framer Model Context Protocol (MCP) server?
faq.answer: Module 07 includes faculty-led architectural exposure to Framer's official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server released on October 22, 2026. Students learn how AI agents programmatically interact with design tokens and CMS schemas without needing to code custom servers.

faq.question: Are expensive paid AI subscriptions required?
faq.answer: No. Free tiers of ChatGPT (GPT-4o mini) and Claude are 100% sufficient for all research and copywriting exercises. Figma and Framer provide free monthly credits. Zero paid AI subscriptions are mandatory.

faq.question: Will students build comprehensive portfolio case studies?
faq.answer: Yes. Students complete 3 canonical modular assessed case studies plus 1 comprehensive Flagship Capstone: (1) Consumer Mobile App UX/UI, (2) Enterprise B2B SaaS Design System, (3) Live Framer Marketing Website with CMS, and (4) Integrated Commercial Product Launch.

faq.question: How does UI/UX Design Professional differ from Creative Design Master?
faq.answer: Creative Design Master is an 8-month multidisciplinary diploma covering 2D graphic design, InDesign packaging dielines, After Effects motion graphics, 3D animation, and basic UI. UI/UX Design Professional is a specialized 5-month program focused 100% on digital product design, advanced Figma systems, usability testing, and live web production in Framer.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee, duration, and applicable GST?
faq.answer: The selling price is flat INR 44,900 (0% artificial discount) for 5 Months (200 guided instructional hours). Statutory 18% GST (INR 8,082) is itemized on all commercial invoices, bringing the total payable fee to INR 52,982. There are zero hidden administrative charges.

faq.question: Are flexible No-Cost EMI payment plans available?
faq.answer: Yes. Approved No-Cost EMI options are available through partner banks: INR 4,415/month for 12 months, INR 6,623/month for 8 months, or INR 8,830/month for 6 months.

faq.question: What verified career and placement assistance does Nova Skills provide?
faq.answer: Nova Skills provides 1-on-1 portfolio case study reviews, 1-page ATS product designer resume optimization, mock technical interview defense coaching, live whiteboarding challenge preparation, and direct recruitment introductions to hiring partner product teams and agencies.

faq.question: Will I own the source files and live websites I create during the course?
faq.answer: Yes. 100% of all Figma design files, FigJam boards, Framer project remix links, and live published `.framer.media` URLs remain your intellectual property for commercial portfolio and freelance presentation purposes.

modules.module_title: UX Research, Problem Framing & Product Strategy
modules.module_purpose: Ground learners in evidence-based human-centered design principles, teaching them how to deconstruct ambiguous business challenges, identify genuine user pain points, formulate research hypotheses, and conduct rigorous qualitative user discovery.
what_you_will_learn: Deconstruct commercial product briefs using the Double Diamond methodology, balancing business viability with user desirability.
Design qualitative research instruments including recruitment screeners, discussion guides, and observational inquiry protocols.
Conduct ethical, unbiased 1-on-1 user interviews and deploy structured quantitative screening surveys using Google Forms.
Synthesize qualitative research in FigJam using affinity mapping, thematic clustering, and empathy mapping (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels).
Construct evidence-based user personas and customer journey maps identifying critical pain points and drop-off moments.
Leverage AI tools (ChatGPT/Claude) for research scaffolding, hypothesis brainstorming, and interview guide drafting under strict human review.

lessons.lesson_title: Double Diamond Framework, Product Thinking & Brief Deconstruction
lessons.what_is_taught: The commercial purpose of UX design: UI vs UX, interaction architecture vs visual styling, and the end-to-end product design lifecycle. Deconstructing client briefs using the Double Diamond model (Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver), balancing business needs against user desirability, and defining UX deliverables across product teams.
subtopics: UI vs UX: defining user experience, interaction architecture, and visual aesthetics
The digital product design lifecycle from initial discovery to commercial delivery
The Double Diamond model: Discover (Divergent), Define (Convergent), Develop (Divergent), Deliver (Convergent)
Human-centered design (HCD) principles and aligning business metrics with user needs
Product discovery fundamentals: assessing technical feasibility, business viability, and user desirability
Industry UX design roles: UX Researcher, Product Designer, UI Designer, and Design Systems Specialist
Anatomy of commercial UX deliverables: discovery decks, user flows, wireframes, and prototypes
lessons.why_it_matters: Jumping directly into visual interface design without problem validation leads to building products that look good but fail in the market. Problem framing ensures teams solve the right problems before solving them right.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze an ambiguous commercial FinTech/HealthTech brief, separate business goals from user needs, and map out a Double Diamond product discovery roadmap.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented Product Discovery Canvas identifying core assumptions, market context, and primary research questions.
lessons.example: Reframing a client request from 'Build a flashy mobile savings app' to 'Reduce financial anxiety for young professionals through automated micro-investing and transparent fee structures.'

lessons.lesson_title: Qualitative User Research, Discussion Guides & Interview Execution
lessons.what_is_taught: Formulating research objectives, qualitative vs quantitative methodologies, and primary vs secondary market research. Authoring unbiased qualitative interview discussion guides, designing recruitment screeners in Google Forms, participant consent, and executing ethical 1-on-1 user interviews.
subtopics: Formulating actionable research objectives and establishing testable UX hypotheses
Qualitative vs quantitative methodologies: when to conduct interviews vs deploy surveys
Primary vs secondary market research and competitive heuristic analysis
Authoring unbiased user interview discussion guides with open-ended inquiry prompts
Designing recruitment screeners in Google Forms with qualifying filters and demographic targets
User recruitment protocols, informed participant consent, and ethical data privacy handling
Observational research and contextual inquiry concepts in real-world user environments
Identifying cognitive research bias: confirmation bias, framing effects, and leading questions
lessons.why_it_matters: Leading questions and biased interviews produce distorted data that misguide product development. Professional qualitative protocols reveal authentic user mental models and underlying emotional drivers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Author an objective 15-question user interview discussion guide, design a Google Forms recruitment screener, and conduct a supervised mock interview simulation.
lessons.expected_outcome: An approved interview discussion guide, screener survey link, and a raw interview transcript capturing verbatim user responses.
lessons.example: Replacing the leading question 'Do you find our current checkout page easy to use?' with the neutral, behavioral question 'Walk me through the last time you completed a purchase online—what worked smoothly, and where did you pause?'

lessons.lesson_title: Research Synthesis, Affinity Mapping & Insight Clustering in FigJam
lessons.what_is_taught: Processing raw interview notes and qualitative data in FigJam. Conducting affinity mapping, clustering data into inductive thematic categories, extracting behavioral patterns, and identifying authentic user pain points. Using AI (ChatGPT/Claude) for research summarization while strictly auditing outputs and enforcing authentic research integrity.
subtopics: Processing raw user interview transcripts, observational notes, and audio logs
Collaborative affinity mapping mechanics in FigJam using tagged digital sticky notes
Divergent grouping: sorting raw observations into bottom-up inductive thematic clusters
Distinguishing empirical evidence from designer assumptions and subjective stakeholder opinions
Identifying behavioral patterns, recurring friction points, and unmet user needs
Using ChatGPT for research synthesis: automated note summarization and theme extraction
Human auditing of AI synthesis: verifying AI suggestions against verbatim interview quotes
Ethical research boundaries: strictly prohibiting fabricated participant responses or synthetic interviews
lessons.why_it_matters: Raw interview transcripts are overwhelming and unmanageable. Affinity mapping systematically condenses dozens of qualitative data points into clear, actionable themes that guide interface architecture.
lessons.what_learner_does: Import 3 user interview transcripts into FigJam, extract 40+ raw observation notes on digital stickies, cluster them into 5 thematic insight pillars, and label key friction patterns.
lessons.expected_outcome: A structured FigJam Affinity Diagram organizing qualitative research into prioritized insight clusters backed by verbatim user evidence.
lessons.example: Clustering 14 disparate complaints about 'forgotten passwords' and 'SMS verification delays' into an overarching behavioral theme: 'High-friction authentication induces cart abandonment during mobile checkout.'

lessons.lesson_title: Validated Personas, Empathy Maps & Customer Journey Mapping
lessons.what_is_taught: Translating synthesized insights into 4-quadrant Empathy Maps, validated user personas, and Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) statements. Formulating actionable Problem Statements using Point of View (POV) formulas and 'How Might We' (HMW) challenge questions. Mapping end-to-end Customer Journey Maps with emotional touchpoints and friction inflection points.
subtopics: Empathy mapping quadrants: what the user Says, Thinks, Does, and Feels during product interactions
Data-driven personas vs fictional proto-personas: anchoring user archetypes in empirical evidence
The Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) framework: 'When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]'
Authoring actionable Problem Statements using Point of View (POV) formulas
Formulating 'How Might We' (HMW) questions to bridge problem definition into creative ideation
End-to-end Customer Journey Mapping: stages, user goals, touchpoints, emotions, and pain points
Identifying service gaps, drop-off inflection points, and high-impact UX opportunity areas
Assembling an executive UX Opportunity Brief with prioritized success metrics
lessons.why_it_matters: Vague target audiences lead to fragmented product features. Validated personas and journey maps unify the entire product team around the user's authentic emotional journey and acute pain points.
lessons.what_learner_does: Construct a 4-quadrant Empathy Map, a validated User Persona card, a 5-stage Customer Journey Map, and 3 prioritized HMW challenge statements in FigJam.
lessons.expected_outcome: A comprehensive UX Strategy Package including Empathy Map, Persona, Journey Map, Problem Statement, and actionable HMW statements.
lessons.example: Mapping a commuter's emotional journey on a transit app: highlighting the peak anxiety drop-off at 'Platform Announcement Mismatch' and framing the HMW: 'How might we deliver real-time, offline-accessible platform alerts within 3 seconds of arrival?'

modules.hands_on_practice: Conduct a small supervised UX research study for a mobile/web product concept: draft an interview guide, run 2 participant interviews, cluster observations in FigJam, and build an empathy map.
modules.assignment: Deliver an end-to-end UX Discovery Report (PDF/FigJam) including research plan, interview guide, screener, 2 verified interview transcripts, FigJam affinity diagram, 1 validated user persona, 1 customer journey map, and 3 How-Might-We statements.
modules.business_application: De-risk early-stage product investments by validating customer pain points before writing code or designing high-fidelity screens, saving hundreds of engineering hours.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 01 UX Research & Problem Framing deliverable package adhering to ethical research standards.

key_concepts: Happy Paths, Decision Nodes & Edge Cases

lessons.what_is_taught: Foundational cognitive psychology in Information Architecture: mental models, cognitive load, Miller's Law (7±2 chunks), and Hick's Law. Conducting open and closed card sorting in FigJam, tree testing introduction, and authoring multi-level hierarchical product sitemaps.
subtopics: Cognitive foundations of Information Architecture: mental models, cognitive load, and scent of information
Core psychological principles in IA: Miller's Law (Chunking 7±2), Hick's Law, and Progressive Disclosure
Feature inventory and content audits: categorizing existing digital product assets
Navigation paradigms: hierarchical, hub-and-spoke, sequential, tabbed, and mega-menus
Card sorting methodologies: open vs closed card sorting in FigJam to discover natural user taxonomies
Introduction to tree testing and validating menu taxonomy findability before visual design
Authoring comprehensive product sitemaps with clear visual hierarchy, page labels, and URL depth
lessons.why_it_matters: A beautiful user interface cannot rescue a poorly structured product. Clear information architecture ensures users find what they need with minimal cognitive friction and zero disorientation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conduct a closed card-sorting session in FigJam with 25 product features, evaluate participant placement agreement, and draft a 3-level hierarchical sitemap for a multi-service mobile application.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented card-sorting synthesis board and a clean 3-tier product sitemap in FigJam.
lessons.example: Restructuring an overwhelming healthcare app menu with 30 unorganized links into 4 distinct, user-validated cognitive buckets: 'Appointments', 'Medical Records', 'Prescriptions', and 'Billing Support'.

lessons.lesson_title: User Flows, Task Analysis & Edge Case Mapping
lessons.what_is_taught: Task analysis, user flows, task flows, screen flows, and wireflows. Standard flowchart symbology (start/end nodes, decision diamonds, actions, system rules). Engineering the primary happy path alongside alternative paths, error handling, onboarding, authentication, and transaction/checkout loops.
subtopics: Task analysis: breaking down complex user goals into atomic operational steps
Differentiating user flows, task flows, screen flows, and wireflows
Standard flowchart symbology: start/end points, screens/pages, decision diamonds, actions, and system logic
Mapping the primary 'happy path' alongside critical decision forks and alternative branches
Error path architecture: handling network failures, validation errors, and invalid inputs gracefully
Core workflow architectures: user onboarding, authentication/registration, search & faceted filtering
Transaction flow architecture: multi-step checkout, booking reservation, and payment confirmation loops
lessons.why_it_matters: Designers who only design ideal 'happy paths' leave engineering teams to guess how error states, empty screens, and system timeouts behave, leading to broken user experiences.
lessons.what_learner_does: Diagram an end-to-end user flow for a mobile checkout/booking experience in FigJam, incorporating 3 decision points, 2 validation error branches, and 1 fallback recovery path.
lessons.expected_outcome: A standardized user flow diagram containing start/end states, clear decision logic, edge cases, and annotated screen triggers.
lessons.example: Mapping an e-commerce credit card transaction flow that accounts for expired card entries, OTP timeout retries, and insufficient funds with contextual recovery prompts.

lessons.what_is_taught: The importance of rapid analog sketching on paper. Running Crazy Eights ideation sprints (8 concepts in 8 minutes), low-fidelity thumbnail compositions, divergent exploration vs convergent selection, and paper prototyping walk-throughs to validate structural layout options.
subtopics: The power of analog ideation: why sketching on paper outperforms designing directly in software
Crazy Eights ideation sprint: forcing 8 distinct layout solutions in 8 minutes
Low-fidelity thumbnail sketching: layout blocks, focal entry points, and structural proportions
Divergent exploration vs convergent selection: evaluating concepts against user flow requirements
Paper prototyping: running quick paper-in-hand user walk-throughs to validate layout intuition
Establishing visual hierarchy on paper: lead headlines, media containers, CTA placements, and navigation bars
lessons.why_it_matters: Sketching rapidly on paper breaks digital design inertia, prevents premature attachment to a single idea, and allows designers to explore multiple unconventional solutions in minutes.
lessons.what_learner_does: Execute a Crazy Eights sketching exercise for a core dashboard screen, select the 2 most viable layout directions, and refine them into detailed paper wireframes.
lessons.expected_outcome: An 8-frame Crazy 8s ideation sheet and 2 annotated low-fidelity paper wireframes ready for digital translation.
lessons.example: Exploring 8 distinct visual arrangements for a mobile banking dashboard—testing bottom sheets, circular progress cards, segmented swipe tabs, and collapsible header widgets.

lessons.lesson_title: Mid-Fidelity Digital Wireframing & UX Microcopy in Figma
lessons.what_is_taught: Constructing structural mid-fidelity wireframes in Figma on 8-column mobile and 12-column desktop frames. Grayscale discipline, content-first wireframing (eliminating lorem ipsum), authoring functional UX microcopy (labels, helper text, error messages), and designing empty/loading/error state variations.
subtopics: Translating paper sketches into digital mid-fidelity wireframes on 8-column mobile and 12-column desktop frames in Figma
Grayscale discipline: eliminating color and stylistic distractions to focus exclusively on layout, spacing, and hierarchy
Content-first wireframing vs lorem ipsum: why realistic copy is essential for accurate layout budgeting
UX writing and microcopy: craft clear form labels, instructional helper text, empty states, and humanized error messages
Structural layout containers: headers, card grids, bottom tab bars, floating action buttons, and modal dialogs
Designing complete screen state variations: default, loading skeleton, empty state, and error message
Wireframe critique and iteration cycles: conducting peer usability walk-throughs to test cognitive clarity
lessons.why_it_matters: Wireframes with placeholder 'Lorem Ipsum' fail during development because real user content has variable lengths and edge cases. Content-first wireframing tests whether layouts hold up in production.
lessons.what_learner_does: Construct a 6-screen mid-fidelity wireframe set in Figma for a core user flow, featuring realistic UX microcopy, skeleton loading states, and an empty state.
lessons.expected_outcome: A Figma canvas containing 6 structured mid-fidelity wireframe screens with annotated microcopy, clear spatial hierarchy, and error/empty state variations.
lessons.example: Replacing generic 'An error occurred' with conversational, actionable microcopy: 'We couldn't verify your phone number. Check that you entered a valid 10-digit number and tap Resend Code.'

modules.hands_on_practice: Create a complete information architecture, user flow diagram, and 6 mid-fidelity wireframe screens in Figma for a mobile app flow with state variations.
modules.assignment: Deliver an Information Architecture & Wireframing Package (PDF/Figma) containing 1 sitemap, 1 branching user flow diagram, and 6 mid-fidelity mobile wireframes covering default, loading, empty, and error states with complete UX microcopy.
modules.business_application: Establish unambiguous product requirements and validated layout logic before visual production, reducing design rework by up to 40%.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 02 deliverables demonstrating logical navigation, clear task flows, and content-first wireframing.

modules.module_purpose: Master the visual, aesthetic, and compositional principles of user interface design, developing fluency with Figma's vector engine, typographic hierarchies, color psychology, and interface layout grids.
what_you_will_learn: Navigate and master the Figma canvas, file structures, pages, frames, sections, layers, and vector networks.
Apply visual design fundamentals (contrast, visual balance, Gestalt laws, focal points) to digital product interfaces.
Construct mathematical modular typographic scales and establish disciplined hierarchy across body, display, and micro-labels.
Formulate accessible semantic color palettes adhering strictly to 60-30-10 distribution and WCAG contrast standards.
Implement the 8pt spatial grid system (and 4pt micro-grid) to maintain mathematical spatial cadence across UI layouts.
Design comprehensive core UI component primitives (buttons, inputs, cards, tabs, modals, badges) across all interactive states.
key_concepts: UI State Variations (Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Loading)

lessons.lesson_title: Figma Interface Architecture, Frames & Vector Mechanics
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the Figma workspace: files, pages, sections, frames, layers, clipping masks, and vector networks. Boolean operations (Union, Subtract, Intersect, Exclude), crafting pixel-perfect 24x24px UI icons, styles management (color, typography, effects), and real-time multiplayer collaboration.
subtopics: Figma workspace architecture: drafts, project folders, files, pages, sections, and canvas navigation
Frames vs Groups vs Sections: why frames are foundational to digital UI composition
Deep dive into Figma layers, z-index hierarchy, clipping masks, and blend modes
Vector networks engine: mastering the Pen tool, Bend tool, anchor points, handles, and path closing
Boolean operations: Union, Subtract, Intersect, and Exclude selection for custom vector shapes
Designing pixel-perfect 24x24px vector UI icons with a strict bounding box and 2px optical stroke weight
Figma styles management: creating, naming, updating, and detaching color and text styles
Canvas collaboration: utilizing real-time multiplayer cursor comments, version history, and named checkpoints
lessons.why_it_matters: Mastering Figma's canvas architecture and vector networks is the baseline technical requirement for any UI designer. Treating frames properly avoids broken layouts and unmanageable layer trees.
lessons.what_learner_does: Set up a clean Figma project file, build 6 custom 24x24px vector icons using boolean operations, and organize file pages with a standardized cover thumbnail.
lessons.expected_outcome: A well-structured Figma file containing custom vector icons, published color/text styles, and a standardized project page structure.
lessons.example: Constructing a shopping bag vector icon inside a 24x24px bounding box using Boolean Subtract to notch the handle and adjusting the Bend tool for optical corner curves.

lessons.lesson_title: 8pt Spatial Cadence, Layout Grids & Gestalt Composition
lessons.what_is_taught: The 8pt spatial grid system and 4pt micro-grid architecture. Establishing layout grids across mobile (4-column), tablet (8-column), and desktop (12-column). Gestalt principles in digital UI (proximity, similarity, continuity), visual balance, optical centering, negative space discipline, and focal scanning vectors (F and Z patterns).
subtopics: The 8pt spatial grid system: mathematical logic, cognitive benefits, and developer alignment
The 4pt micro-grid: scaling typography, icons, and micro-padding elements with precision
Layout grids across breakpoints: 4-column mobile grids (16px margins), 8-column tablet, 12-column desktop (24px gutters)
Applying Gestalt principles to UI composition: proximity for card grouping, similarity for clickable elements, continuity for lists
Visual balance: symmetrical vs asymmetrical weighting, optical center vs geometric center
Negative space (white space) as an intentional layout element to reduce cognitive friction and highlight primary actions
Focal hierarchy: guiding user attention using scale contrast, tonal weight, and reading scanning vectors (F and Z patterns)
lessons.why_it_matters: Arbitrary spacing (e.g. 7px, 13px, 22px) makes interfaces look sloppy and amateurish while infuriating developers. An 8pt spatial grid ensures visual rhythm, harmony, and effortless code translation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Take an unaligned, cluttered mobile screen and refactor it onto a strict 4-column 8pt spatial grid, enforcing consistent 8px/16px/24px/32px spacing intervals throughout.
lessons.expected_outcome: A refactored mobile UI screen demonstrating rigorous 8pt spatial cadence, clean alignment, and intentional negative space.
lessons.example: Aligning a product card's internal padding to 16px, image-to-title gap to 12px (4pt micro-step), title-to-description to 8px, and card-to-card margin to 16px.

lessons.lesson_title: UI Typography Systems, Modular Scales & Text Hierarchy
lessons.what_is_taught: Typography architecture for user interfaces: selecting workhorse digital typefaces, constructing modular scales (Major Third, Perfect Fourth), establishing 7-level typographic hierarchies, optical line-height (leading), letter-spacing (tracking), line length constraints (measure), and mobile legibility standards.
subtopics: UI typography fundamentals: legibility vs readability, font classification, and selecting workhorse interface typefaces
Constructing modular typographic scales: Major Second (1.125), Minor Third (1.200), Major Third (1.250), Perfect Fourth (1.333)
Establishing a complete 7-level type hierarchy: Display, H1, H2, H3, Body-Large, Body-Regular, Caption/Overline
Optical line-height (leading) rules: tighter leading for display headlines (110–120%), relaxed leading for body text (140–160%)
Letter-spacing (tracking) adjustments: negative tracking for large titles, positive tracking for uppercase micro-labels
Measure and line length: constraining body text to optimal 45–75 characters per line for maximum reading comprehension
Mobile text hierarchy: optimizing touch screen legibility and minimum accessible font sizes (16px base body font)
Button and label typography: casing, weight, vertical alignment, and icon-to-text spatial pairing
lessons.why_it_matters: Interface design is 90% typography. A disciplined type scale immediately communicates content hierarchy, guides the user's reading eye, and elevates product polish to enterprise standards.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a complete typography style sheet in Figma using a Major Third modular scale, define responsive line-heights and letter-spacing, and typeset a content-heavy article screen.
lessons.expected_outcome: A published Figma typography style library and a typeset mobile screen demonstrating impeccable typographic hierarchy and readability.
lessons.example: Setting an 18px body font with 28px line-height (155%) for comfortable scanning, while setting a 32px headline with 38px line-height (118%) and -0.02em tracking.

lessons.lesson_title: Color Palettes, UI States & Visual Polish
lessons.what_is_taught: UI color theory, 60-30-10 distribution, semantic palettes (Primary, Secondary, Neutrals, Success, Warning, Error, Info), and accessible HSL tint curves. Engineering realistic multi-layer drop shadows and elevation depth. Designing core UI elements across all interaction states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error).
subtopics: Color theory in product interfaces: psychological impact, cultural associations, and brand alignment
The 60-30-10 visual distribution rule: 60% dominant neutral background, 30% structural secondary, 10% high-impact accent
Architecting a functional UI palette: Primary brand, Secondary, Neutral grays (9 tints/shades), and Semantic states (Success, Warning, Error, Info)
Generating accessible color tints using HSL/HCL lightness curves rather than arbitrary opacity blending
Elevation and depth: crafting multi-layered realistic drop shadows with ambient diffusion and directional light
Core UI element design: buttons, input fields, dropdowns, navigation bars, cards, tabs, and modal sheets
UI state variations: default, hover, focused (keyboard focus ring), active/pressed, disabled, loading skeleton, and error
Visual UI review checklist: pixel alignment, contrast audit, spacing verification, and design critique preparation
lessons.why_it_matters: Interfaces that only design default states break down when real users hover, click, encounter input errors, or experience slow network loading. Designing state variations is the hallmark of a professional UI designer.
lessons.what_learner_does: Convert approved low-fidelity wireframes into 3 polished, high-fidelity mobile UI screens featuring buttons, inputs, and cards across all interaction states.
lessons.expected_outcome: Three high-fidelity mobile UI screens in Figma accompanied by an interactive UI state variation sheet and documented color/typography tokens.
lessons.example: Designing an input field that clearly displays Default (gray border), Focus (2px primary blue ring + floating label), Filled (dark text), Error (red border + helper text), and Disabled (muted gray surface).

modules.hands_on_practice: Convert approved low-fidelity wireframes into high-fidelity mobile UI screens in Figma adhering to the 8pt grid, modular type scale, and semantic color rules.
modules.assignment: Deliver a High-Fidelity Mobile UI Suite (Figma file) consisting of 3 finished screens (Feed, Detail, Checkout), an 8pt spatial grid guide, a complete color/type style system, and UI state variations for core interactive components.
modules.business_application: Deliver polished, accessible visual interface designs that boost brand trust, improve visual clarity, and reduce user drop-off in commercial applications.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 03 high-fidelity screen designs exhibiting exceptional visual quality, typographic hierarchy, and design consistency.

modules.module_title: Advanced Figma, Auto Layout & Responsive Components
modules.module_purpose: Elevate Figma proficiency to elite engineering standards, mastering Auto Layout v5, complex component architecture, multi-axis variants, interactive component properties, and scalable responsive structures.
what_you_will_learn: Construct bulletproof, fluid layouts using nested Auto Layout (Horizontal, Vertical, Wrap, Padding, Gap, Alignment).
Master dynamic resizing constraints: Hug Contents, Fill Container, Fixed Width/Height, and Min/Max dimension limits.
Implement absolute positioning within Auto Layout frames for floating badges, notification pips, and overlapping avatars.
Engineer modular master components utilizing Boolean visibility, text content, and instance swap component properties.
Architect multi-dimensional component sets and variants covering all interactive states without unnecessary variant bloat.
Create responsive layouts across Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile breakpoints, understanding honest Figma resizing behavior vs Framer.
Implement Figma Variables (Color, Number, String, Boolean) and build light/dark mode theme switching.
key_concepts: Auto Layout v5 Mechanics (Direction, Hug, Fill, Fixed)
Responsive Navigation Adaptation (Desktop Bar vs Mobile Drawer)
Honest Figma Resizing vs Code-Backed Viewport Engines

lessons.lesson_title: Auto Layout v5 Architecture, Nested Frames & Fluid Reflow
lessons.what_is_taught: In-depth Auto Layout mechanics: Horizontal, Vertical, and Wrap modes. Padding, gap, alignment matrices, Hug vs Fill vs Fixed dimensions, min/max dimension constraints, absolute positioning within Auto Layout, negative spacing for avatar stacks, and fluid reflow under dynamic content changes.
subtopics: Auto Layout core mental model: flexbox-inspired layout mechanics in a visual canvas
Layout directions: Horizontal row, Vertical column, and Auto Layout Wrap for dynamic chip and tag clouds
Spatial controls: individual padding (top, right, bottom, left), gap spacing, and alignment matrix
Sizing behaviors: Hug Contents (shrink-wrap), Fill Container (fluid expansion), and Fixed dimensions
Setting Minimum and Maximum widths and heights (`min-width`, `max-width`, `min-height`, `max-height`) for fluid containers
Absolute positioning inside Auto Layout frames: pinning floating notification badges and close buttons
Negative space control and negative spacing for overlapping avatar stacks (`-space-between` and stack order)
Stress-testing nested layouts: verifying that cards expand and reflow gracefully when headline copy changes from 1 to 4 lines
lessons.why_it_matters: Static frames break the moment content changes or screens resize. Auto Layout ensures UI components behave like real code, expanding, wrapping, and reflowing dynamically to handle real-world content variations.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build an enterprise dashboard card containing avatar, status tag, title, metric counter, and action buttons entirely out of nested Auto Layout frames that fluidly adjust from 320px to 600px width.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully fluid Auto Layout card component that handles arbitrary text changes and width resizes without breaking alignment.
lessons.example: Configuring a pricing card where the price tag uses Hug Contents, the feature description uses Fill Container with a max-width of 400px, and the container automatically adjusts height when features are added.

lessons.lesson_title: Master Components, Component Properties & Variant Sets
lessons.what_is_taught: Master components vs instances, component property architecture (Boolean, Text, Instance Swap), and multi-dimensional variant matrices. Eliminating variant bloat, stateful component sets (Default, Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Loading, Error), nesting atomic components into molecules, and library maintenance.
subtopics: Component fundamentals: Main component (master) vs Instances and understanding safe overrides
Component sets and multi-dimensional variant matrices: combining Type, Size, State, and Theme
Component properties: Boolean properties (toggling icon visibility), Text properties (editing label strings), and Instance Swap properties (swapping icon glyphs)
Eliminating variant bloat: using component properties to reduce a 128-variant button set down to a clean 16-variant matrix
Stateful components: engineering Default, Hover, Focused, Active/Pressed, Disabled, Loading, and Error states
Nesting atomic components into complex molecular components (e.g. assembling Button + Input + Label into a Search Bar)
Component library organization, naming conventions (Slash naming vs property naming), and publishing to team libraries
lessons.why_it_matters: Without component properties and disciplined variant architectures, Figma design files explode into thousands of unmaintainable duplicate layers. Modern component engineering creates lean, scalable design systems.
lessons.what_learner_does: Engineer a production-ready Master Button component set in Figma with 3 sizes (Small, Medium, Large), 4 types (Primary, Secondary, Outline, Ghost), 5 interaction states, and Boolean icon properties.
lessons.expected_outcome: A clean, published Figma Component Set featuring Boolean and Instance Swap properties, fully tested across all interactive states.
lessons.example: Building a single Master Input Field that toggles an optional helper text via Boolean property, allows instant icon swapping via Instance Swap, and displays clean Focus/Error states without altering layer names.

lessons.lesson_title: Figma Variables, Token Hierarchy & Light/Dark Theming
lessons.what_is_taught: Figma Variables for design tokens: Color, Number (spacing/radii), String, and Boolean variables. Token hierarchies: Primitive values vs Semantic functional aliases vs Component tokens. Configuring variable modes (Light Mode and Dark Mode), instant theme switching, and variable scoping.
subtopics: Introduction to Figma Variables: defining live data tokens for Color, Number, String, and Boolean
Token hierarchy: Global primitives (`blue-500: #3B82F6`) vs Semantic tokens (`surface-brand-primary: blue-500`) vs Component tokens (`button-bg: surface-brand-primary`)
Number variables: standardizing spatial padding scales (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32px) and border radii (4, 8, 16, 999px)
Variable modes: configuring Light Mode and Dark Mode variable collections
Switching variable modes across frames, sections, and entire page layouts with a single click
String variables: setting up multi-language text strings and localized mock content
Token management hygiene: organizing variable collections, aliases, and scoping variables to specific layer properties
lessons.why_it_matters: Hard-coded hex codes and arbitrary pixel values prevent product scaling. Design tokens and Figma Variables bridge design and frontend engineering, enabling instant light/dark theming and cross-platform token synchronization.
lessons.what_learner_does: Create a complete variable collection in Figma with primitive and semantic color tokens, bind them to a UI screen, and establish Light and Dark mode variations that toggle seamlessly.
lessons.expected_outcome: A multi-mode Figma variable collection and an interactive screen demonstration that toggles between Light and Dark themes with zero contrast errors.
lessons.example: Binding a card background to `surface-primary` which resolves to `#FFFFFF` in Light Mode and `#1E293B` in Dark Mode, while `text-primary` automatically shifts from `#0F172A` to `#F8FAFC`.

lessons.what_is_taught: Responsive layout design across Desktop (1440px), Tablet (768px), and Mobile (390px). Stacking rules, fluid containers, and responsive navigation adaptation (horizontal bar to mobile hamburger drawer). Honest Figma resizing behavior vs code-backed Framer viewports, avoiding false claims regarding automatic variant swapping on resize, and exposure to Figma Sites.
subtopics: Responsive web principles: understanding common viewport breakpoints: Mobile (390px), Tablet (768px), Desktop (1440px)
Fluid layouts vs adaptive layouts: column reflow, stacking rules, and responsive image scaling
Responsive navigation architecture: adapting desktop horizontal navigation bars into mobile bottom tab bars and slide-out drawers
Honest Figma resizing behavior: understanding what Auto Layout can do natively (fluid stretching, wrapping) versus what requires dedicated breakpoint variants
Dispelling false claims: why standard Figma canvas does not automatically swap arbitrary component variants upon frame resize without dedicated breakpoint plugins or Framer
Designing breakpoint-specific layout frames: assembling side-by-side Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile views of the same page
Interactive prototype transitions for responsive menus: prototyping hamburger menu slide-in, overlay backdrop, and close interactions
Exposure to Figma Sites: exploring Figma's evolving native web publishing and breakpoint-aware variant capabilities
lessons.why_it_matters: A desktop interface will fail completely on a mobile viewport if not architected responsively. Understanding the authentic capabilities and limits of Figma ensures designers build practical specs, preparing them for true code-backed web publishing in Framer.
lessons.what_learner_does: Design a complete responsive marketing page section (Hero + Navigation + Feature Grid) across Desktop (1440px), Tablet (768px), and Mobile (390px), including an interactive mobile menu prototype.
lessons.expected_outcome: A 3-breakpoint responsive layout in Figma with interactive mobile menu prototype and documented component reflow rules.
lessons.example: Demonstrating how a 4-column desktop pricing card grid stacks cleanly into a 2x2 grid on tablet and a single-column swipeable carousel on mobile, while the desktop top-bar nav transitions into an accessible mobile bottom sheet.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a reusable responsive website component library in Figma: header, buttons, cards, forms, navigation, dropdown, tabs, pricing card, modal, and footer with Auto Layout and Variables.
modules.assignment: Deliver a Responsive Component Library & Screen Kit in Figma containing 10 master components (Header, Button, Card, Form, Navigation, Dropdown, Tabs, Pricing Card, Modal, Footer) with variant states, design tokens/variables, and a responsive 3-breakpoint layout example.
modules.business_application: Accelerate product team design velocity by up to 5x with reusable, engineering-ready responsive components that reduce developer handoff bugs and design debt.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 04 responsive component library demonstrating rigorous Auto Layout v5, tokenized variables, and multi-breakpoint layout adaptation.

modules.module_purpose: Train students to think like systems architects, creating scalable design tokens, managing multidimensional Figma Variables, enforcing WCAG 2.2 accessibility standards, and conducting flawless developer handoffs.
what_you_will_learn: Architect comprehensive design system foundations following Atomic Design principles (atoms, molecules, organisms, templates).
Formulate comprehensive design token architectures spanning primitive values, semantic aliases, and component-scoped variables.
Audit interface designs against international WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards (contrast ratios, touch targets, focus states).
Design for inclusive digital experiences, incorporating screen-reader focus orders, cognitive accessibility, and localization expansion.
Utilize Figma Dev Mode for code inspection (CSS, Swift, Kotlin), measurement specs, and developer annotations.
Establish design system governance, version history, component changelogs, and team publishing workflows.
key_concepts: Design System vs UI Kit vs Style Guide
Color Contrast Ratios (4.5:1 Body, 3:1 Large Text/UI)
Technical Handoff Specs, Asset Export & QA Auditing

lessons.lesson_title: Design System Architecture, Foundations & Token Governance
lessons.what_is_taught: UI kits vs living design systems, Atomic Design methodology, and foundational design pillars. Component anatomy, naming conventions, comprehensive usage documentation (dos and don'ts), component lifecycle governance (Proposed, Beta, Production, Deprecated), and managing team library updates in Figma.
subtopics: Differentiating UI Kits, Style Guides, and Living Design Systems
Atomic Design methodology: structuring systems from atoms (tokens) to organisms and templates
Foundational design pillars: brand principles, color systems, typography scales, elevation, and spacing scales
Component anatomy: naming conventions, layer structures, documentation frames, and property guidelines
Design system documentation: writing clear component usage rules, dos and don'ts, and edge-case behaviors
Design system governance: component lifecycle (Proposed, Beta, Production, Deprecated), contribution models, and changelogs
Publishing and managing team libraries in Figma: versioning updates and managing component migrations
lessons.why_it_matters: Without system governance, large product teams produce conflicting designs, duplicate code, and inconsistent user experiences. A living design system acts as the single source of truth across product, design, and engineering.
lessons.what_learner_does: Architect a foundational Design System Guidelines board in Figma documenting color tokens, typography scales, spacing rules, and a fully annotated Master Button anatomy sheet with dos and don'ts.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented Design System Foundation file in Figma with clear architectural guidelines, token specifications, and component governance rules.
lessons.example: Documenting that the Primary Action Button must only appear once per viewport, must never be used for destructive actions, and must maintain 16px minimum horizontal internal padding.

lessons.lesson_title: WCAG 2.2 Digital Accessibility Standards & In-Canvas Auditing
lessons.what_is_taught: The Four Principles of WCAG (POUR), WCAG 2.2 AA standards, and contrast ratio formulas (4.5:1 body, 3:1 UI components). Using Stark and in-canvas scanners, color vision deficiency simulation (Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia), touch target minimums (48x48px Android, 44x44px iOS), visible keyboard focus rings, and form error accessibility.
subtopics: Introduction to digital accessibility and the Four Principles of WCAG (POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust)
WCAG 2.2 AA standards: contrast ratio requirements (minimum 4.5:1 for body copy, 3:1 for large text and UI components)
Using Stark and in-canvas plugins to perform automated color contrast scans and identify violations
Color vision deficiency testing: simulating Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, and Achromatopsia
Touch target ergonomics: enforcing minimum 48x48px tap targets on Android and 44x44px on iOS with adequate spacing
Keyboard navigation: designing prominent, accessible focus states and visible focus indicators for all interactive elements
Form accessibility: persistent labels, clear error identification, instructional text, and error prevention confirmation dialogs
Screen reader awareness: annotating heading levels (H1–H6), alternative text (alt text), and reading order
lessons.why_it_matters: Accessibility is a fundamental civil right and legal mandate in modern software. Over 15% of global users experience disabilities; accessible design improves usability for everyone and protects businesses from legal liability.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conduct a comprehensive WCAG 2.2 AA audit on a 6-screen design file using Stark, document all contrast/touch target violations, and implement remediated accessible designs.
lessons.expected_outcome: An Accessibility Audit & Remediation Report with verified passing WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios and annotated focus order specs.
lessons.example: Remediating a muted gray placeholder text with a failing 2.4:1 contrast ratio by adjusting the HSL value to achieve a certified 4.8:1 ratio, while adding an explicit visual label above the input field.

lessons.lesson_title: Inclusive Design, Cognitive Ergonomics & Layout Localization
lessons.what_is_taught: Inclusive design methodologies, cognitive ergonomics (reducing cognitive overload, dyslexia considerations), and reduced motion settings. Localization and internationalization (i18n): handling up to 40% text expansion (e.g. German), Right-to-Left (RTL) layout mirroring considerations, and designing accessible, reassuring error recovery screens.
subtopics: Inclusive UX: designing for diverse cognitive, sensory, physical, and situational capabilities
Cognitive ergonomics: reducing cognitive overload, avoiding unexpected layout shifts, and supporting users with ADHD or dyslexia
Reduced motion preferences: designing subtle, non-triggering transitions for users with vestibular disorders
Mobile accessibility: reachability, thumb zones, dynamic type scaling, and orientation adaptability
Localization and internationalization (i18n): preparing interface layouts for German/Finnish text expansion (up to 40% longer strings)
Right-to-Left (RTL) layout mirroring: architectural considerations for Arabic and Hebrew language interfaces
Accessible error recovery: ensuring errors are clearly explained in plain language with immediate, low-stress resolution paths
Readable content design: plain language guidelines, content chunking, and screen-reader cognitive flow
lessons.why_it_matters: Products built solely for the designer's primary language and device break when localized globally or used by diverse populations. Inclusive design ensures software functions gracefully across cultures and abilities.
lessons.what_learner_does: Stress-test a checkout flow layout against German text expansion (35% string expansion) and design an accessible error recovery screen with clear corrective microcopy.
lessons.expected_outcome: A stress-tested layout showing resilient Auto Layout reflow under localized text expansion and an inclusive error recovery state.
lessons.example: Ensuring an e-commerce 'Add to Cart' button uses Auto Layout with Hug Contents and flexible padding so that the German translation 'In den Warenkorb legen' expands without truncating or clipping.

lessons.lesson_title: Dev Mode Handoff, Technical Redlining & Production Specs
lessons.what_is_taught: Figma Dev Mode for code inspection (CSS box model, Swift, Kotlin), measurement overlays, and asset export presets (SVG, 1x/2x/3x WebP/PNG). Authoring developer annotations, padding/spacing redlines, interaction specs, W3C design token standards, design QA reviews, and early engineering collaboration.
subtopics: Bridging the designer-developer divide: empathetic collaboration between product designers and frontend engineers
Figma Dev Mode deep dive: code inspection (CSS box model, Swift, Kotlin), measurement overlays, and asset export presets
Authoring technical developer annotations: documenting padding, spacing tokens, responsive breakpoint triggers, and interaction states
Asset production and export hygiene: generating clean SVG vectors, 1x/2x/3x WebP/PNG raster assets, and optimizing file sizes
Design token export: inspecting token variables and understanding JSON design token formats (W3C Design Token Community Group)
Documenting micro-interactions and transitions: specifying ease curves, durations (150ms–300ms), and spring physics
Design QA (Quality Assurance): conducting design reviews on staging builds to identify and log design-to-implementation mismatches
Technical feasibility reviews: discussing constraints with engineers early to avoid late-stage redesigns
lessons.why_it_matters: A design that cannot be accurately built by developers provides zero business value. Professional Dev Mode handoff with unambiguous annotations ensures pixel-perfect engineering execution.
lessons.what_learner_does: Set up a complete Figma Dev Mode handoff board for a 4-screen flow, authoring developer annotations, spacing redlines, interaction specs, and exportable asset packages.
lessons.expected_outcome: A production-ready Figma Dev Mode Handoff package with comprehensive developer annotations, exported assets, and token documentation.
lessons.example: Annotating a responsive card component in Dev Mode specifying: `padding: var(--space-4)`, `border-radius: var(--radius-md)`, hover transition: `200ms ease-out`, and export assets configured at `@1x`, `@2x`, and `SVG`.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create a documented reusable design system foundation, conduct a WCAG 2.2 accessibility audit, and build a developer handoff specification in Figma.
modules.assignment: Deliver a Design System & Developer Handoff Package (Figma file) containing: 1 Design System Foundations page (color tokens, typography scale, spacing variables), 1 WCAG 2.2 AA Accessibility Audit sheet, and 1 complete Dev Mode Handoff spec with developer annotations and asset exports.
modules.business_application: Eliminate communication friction between design and engineering, reduce developer implementation time by 30%, and guarantee full legal compliance with digital accessibility mandates.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 05 deliverables demonstrating systemic token design, rigorous accessibility auditing, and production-grade developer handoff specifications.

modules.module_purpose: Bring static user interfaces to life through high-fidelity interactive prototyping, variable-driven conditional logic, realistic micro-interactions, and validating design decisions through unmoderated and moderated usability testing.
what_you_will_learn: Master Figma prototyping triggers (On click, On hover, While pressing, Mouse enter/leave, After delay) and actions.
Implement physics-based Smart Animate transitions, custom Bézier easing curves, and stateful micro-interactions.
Build advanced dynamic prototypes utilizing Figma Variables, conditional logic (If/Else), and interactive inputs.
Engineer complex scroll behaviors including sticky headers, nested scrolling frames, and horizontal carousels.
Author unmoderated and moderated usability testing protocols, scenario tasks, and recruitment screeners in Maze.
Analyze quantitative usability data (Task Success Rate, Time on Task, Misclick Heatmaps, SUS Scores) and synthesize actionable design iterations.
key_concepts: System Usability Scale (SUS) & Task Completion Rates

lessons.lesson_title: Core Prototyping, Overlays & Smart Animate Dynamics
lessons.what_is_taught: Interaction design fundamentals: affordances, signifiers, feedback loops, and progressive disclosure. Prototyping connections in Figma: screen-to-screen navigation, contextual modal overlays, and back navigation. Smart Animate mechanics: matching layer names for seamless morphing, physics-based easing curves (Ease-in, Ease-out, Ease-in-out, Custom Bézier), and micro-interaction timing.
subtopics: Interaction design principles: user control, feedback loops, affordances, and cognitive signifiers
Configuring Figma prototype triggers: On click, On hover, While pressing, Mouse enter/leave, and Key/gamepad
Modal and drawer overlays: centering, bottom-sheet slide-up, backdrop dimming, and close-on-click-outside
Smart Animate physics: layer matching hierarchy, scale morphing, and path interpolation rules
Custom Bézier easing curves: configuring snappy 200ms–350ms curves for interface feedback
Micro-interaction labs: designing animated toggle switches, interactive button loaders, and like counter badges
Accessibility in motion: WCAG 2.2 reduced-motion preferences and avoiding vestibular triggers
lessons.why_it_matters: Static screens cannot communicate the emotional feel or temporal responsiveness of an application. Smart Animate and thoughtful micro-interactions provide clear visual feedback, reassuring users that their inputs were registered.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build an interactive 4-screen flow in Figma with modal overlays, bottom sheets, and Smart Animate toggle switches using custom Bézier curves.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fluid Figma prototype featuring smooth screen transitions, interactive overlays, and realistic micro-interactions.
lessons.example: Configuring a shopping cart drawer that slides in from the right with a 300ms ease-out curve while darkening the underlying background with a 40% black backdrop overlay.

lessons.what_is_taught: Advanced dynamic prototyping in Figma using Variables and conditional logic. Binding number variables to persistent cart counters, evaluating If/Else conditions, setting string variables for dynamic text input simulation, handling multi-step form validation, and engineering sticky/fixed elements, scroll-to anchors, and nested horizontal carousels.
subtopics: Figma Variables in prototypes: manipulating Number, String, and Boolean variables dynamically
Setting variable expressions: incrementing/decrementing quantities and calculating running subtotals
Conditional interactions (If/Else): validating inputs and disabling submit buttons when required fields are empty
Simulating dynamic form inputs: typing states, password reveal toggles, and contextual error banners
Sticky and fixed UI patterns: locking top navigation bars and floating action buttons during vertical scroll
Nested scroll containers: creating horizontal swipeable card carousels within a vertically scrolling page
Scroll-to interactions: smooth-scrolling to specific page sections upon anchor link triggers
lessons.why_it_matters: Traditional prototypes require hundreds of duplicate screens to simulate simple variable states. Using Figma variables and conditional logic allows designers to build realistic, data-driven prototypes with a fraction of the screens.
lessons.what_learner_does: Engineer an e-commerce product detail and cart prototype in Figma that increments item counts, recalculates total price via variables, and conditionally disables the checkout button if total quantity is zero.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully functional variable-driven Figma prototype simulating realistic cart calculations and conditional validation logic.
lessons.example: Setting a conditional rule: 'If cartCount > 0, set button state to Active and navigate to Checkout; Else, show inline toast notification: Your cart is empty.'

lessons.lesson_title: Usability Testing Protocols, Task Scenarios & Maze Configuration
lessons.what_is_taught: Usability testing methodology: formulating research hypotheses, moderated vs unmoderated testing, authoring unbiased task scenarios, and defining quantitative metrics (Task Success Rate, Time on Task, Misclick Rate, System Usability Scale). Connecting Figma prototypes to Maze, establishing test missions, and deploying recruitment screeners.
subtopics: Formulating usability research questions: identifying high-risk interaction assumptions before launch
Moderated testing protocols: think-aloud protocol, non-leading facilitation, and observational inquiry
Unmoderated testing architecture: designing self-guided testing missions with objective pass/fail criteria
Writing unbiased task scenarios: providing realistic context without hinting at exact interface buttons
Connecting Figma prototypes to Maze: setting up missions, defining expected paths, and setting success screens
Quantitative metrics in usability: Task Completion Rate, Time on Task, Misclick Rate, and Path Bounce Rate
The System Usability Scale (SUS): administering the standard 10-item questionnaire and scoring benchmarks
lessons.why_it_matters: Designers cannot evaluate their own work objectively. Testing interactive prototypes with unbiased users exposes unexpected friction points, confusing navigation terminology, and cognitive drop-offs before engineering begins.
lessons.what_learner_does: Write a 3-scenario usability test plan, connect their variable-driven Figma prototype to Maze, configure missions with defined success paths, and launch an unmoderated study with 5 participants.
lessons.expected_outcome: An active Maze usability testing study with verified prototype integration, clear scenario prompts, and automated tracking metrics.
lessons.example: Authoring the scenario: 'You want to order groceries for dinner tonight. Find a pack of organic avocados and add them to your cart,' avoiding the leading phrase 'Tap the green Add to Cart button on the fruit card.'

lessons.lesson_title: Usability Data Synthesis, Heatmap Analysis & Iterative Refinement
lessons.what_is_taught: Synthesizing usability test results: analyzing Maze click heatmaps, user misclick hotspots, and drop-off funnels. Calculating normalized SUS scores, categorizing findings by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low), authoring an executive Usability Audit Report, and executing verified iterative design improvements.
subtopics: Analyzing Maze analytical output: heatmaps, click paths, misclick percentages, and user drop-off points
Differentiating usability flaws from user preference feedback and cosmetic critiques
Severity assessment matrix: evaluating issue frequency, task criticality, and persistence
Calculating and interpreting System Usability Scale (SUS) scores against industry percentiles (Average: 68)
Synthesizing qualitative user commentary into prioritized remediation recommendations
Authoring an executive Usability Test Report documenting methodology, key metrics, and evidence
Executing design iteration rounds: modifying layout, microcopy, and affordances based on empirical data
Validating redesigned screens and annotating final design changes for developer handoff
lessons.why_it_matters: Collecting usability data is useless without disciplined synthesis. Prioritizing issues by severity ensures product teams fix catastrophic blockers first, transforming empirical user feedback into measurable product improvements.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze testing data from 5 Maze sessions, calculate the average SUS score, author a 4-page Usability Audit Report with heatmap screenshots, and implement 3 verified design fixes in Figma.
lessons.expected_outcome: A comprehensive Usability Audit Report and an updated, refined Figma prototype addressing all identified user friction points.
lessons.example: Discovering an 80% misclick rate on an unclickable card image, and resolving it by adding an explicit 'View Details' text link with an arrow icon and expanding the interactive tap target to the entire card container.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create an interactive product prototype with working navigation, interactive menu, modal overlays, scroll interactions, and conditional variable logic, and run a supervised usability test in Maze.
modules.assignment: Deliver an Interaction & Usability Package consisting of: (1) An advanced interactive Figma prototype with variables and conditional states, (2) A complete Usability Test Plan, (3) Maze testing analytics with click heatmaps, and (4) An executive Usability Audit & Iteration Report documenting empirical findings and final design refinements.
modules.business_application: Validate complex interactive workflows before engineering, eliminate costly usability defects, and ensure product release meets international usability benchmarks (SUS > 80).
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 06 deliverables demonstrating high-fidelity interaction mechanics, empirical usability validation, and iterative design refinement.

modules.module_title: Framer Website Design, CMS, Motion & Publishing
modules.module_purpose: Equip product designers with real-world visual web publishing capabilities, teaching them how to translate Figma UI concepts into production-ready responsive websites in Framer featuring native CMS collections, scroll effects, SEO optimization, and live domain deployment.

Execute seamless Figma-to-Framer asset migrations, refactoring static frames into clean web layouts.
Build fully responsive websites across Desktop (1200px+), Tablet (810px), and Mobile (390px) breakpoints.
Engineer a functional responsive navigation bar that automatically switches to a mobile hamburger drawer upon viewport resize.
Architect and populate dynamic Framer CMS collections for case studies, blogs, and marketing resources.
Configure production-grade scroll transforms, scroll-triggered entrance reveals, and interactive component variants.
Deploy live, SEO-optimized, accessible websites to `.framer.media` with functional contact forms.

Framer CMS Collections & Dynamic Detail Page Templating
Functional Forms, Spam Prevention & Submission Endpoints
On-Page SEO Optimization, Open Graph & Accessibility Checks

Framer Model Context Protocol (MCP) Architectural Exposure

Preparing Figma files for import, using the official Figma-to-Framer plugin, diagnosing layout anomalies, resolving font mismatches, and rebuilding static layers into clean web-standard structural hierarchies.

Stacks and Grids: mastering direction, wrap, distributed alignment, padding, and gap spacing
Positioning models in Framer: Relative, Absolute, Fixed, and Sticky positioning rules
Preparing Figma designs for migration: flattening raster assets, naming layers, and grouping Auto Layout frames
Using the Figma-to-Framer plugin: pasting layers into Framer and resolving import anomalies
Rebuilding static vectors into native Framer layout containers and verifying font consistency
Framer project structure: managing pages, reusable text/color styles, and global asset libraries

lessons.expected_outcome: A clean, error-free Framer project file containing a fully refactored desktop marketing homepage layout.
