lessons.lesson_title: Composition, Visual Hierarchy & Layout Systems in Motion
lessons.what_is_taught: Visual communication fundamentals for video canvases: composition, framing, rule of thirds, golden ratio, and visual rhythm. Building responsive 8pt layout systems for 1920x1080 (landscape) and 1080x1920 (vertical reels). Enforcing EBU/SMPTE broadcast title-safe (80%) and action-safe (90%) margins, as well as mobile social UI overlay zones. Establishing visual hierarchy through scale, contrast, weight, spacing and alignment, and negative space to direct viewer attention across frames. Establishing brand consistency through colour theory, tint/shade systems, and accessible contrast ratios.
subtopics: Composition rules: rule of thirds, golden ratio, balance, and visual rhythm across moving frames
Layout systems and 8pt design grid architecture adapted to 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 motion graphics canvases
Spacing and alignment: calibrating padding, margins, and negative space across multi-element layouts
Title-safe and action-safe boundaries (EBU R95 and SMPTE ST 2048) versus modern social media safe zones
Visual hierarchy: controlling viewer eye path using scale contrast, tonal weight, and focal points
Colour theory and brand consistency: establishing motion palettes, tint/shade variations, and contrast ratios
lessons.why_it_matters: Poor layout and hierarchy result in cluttered, unreadable frames where viewers miss key commercial messages.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs an 8pt motion grid template in Illustrator and designs 3 balanced composition layouts incorporating safe margins, spacing and alignment, and brand guidelines.
lessons.expected_outcome: Three grid-aligned motion composition layouts complying with broadcast and social media safe zones.
lessons.example: Setting up a title card layout where the brand logo, headline, and legal disclaimer remain within 80% title-safe zones on both broadcast monitors and mobile phones.

lessons.what_is_taught: Type anatomy and selection for time-based media: geometric sans-serifs vs humanists vs modern serifs. Typographic hierarchy: title, subtitle, body copy, and metadata styling. Kerning, tracking, line length, and leading for fast video readability. Applying foundational motion principles to graphic layouts: timing and spacing, anticipation and follow-through, squash and stretch awareness, and easing and motion curves. Translating static typographic layouts into dynamic time-based choreography with predictable readability dwell times.
subtopics: Typeface selection and typography for motion: evaluating legibility, stroke weight consistency, and pixel rendering at speed
Tracking, kerning, and leading calibration for moving text to prevent vibration and visual stutter
Motion principles in design: understanding timing and spacing to give graphical weight to UI and typographic elements
Anticipation and follow-through: designing layout cues that signal impending movement and kinetic energy
Squash and stretch awareness: planning deformable graphics versus rigid geometric shapes
Easing and motion curves: conceptualizing acceleration, deceleration, and velocity profiles before entering software
lessons.why_it_matters: Moving typography requires vastly higher contrast and tighter spacing than print; understanding motion principles prevents mechanical-looking animation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs a typographic motion board testing kerning, tracking, and readability at 24fps and 60fps across three font weights with planned motion curves.
lessons.expected_outcome: A typographic motion style sheet defining fonts, sizes, tracking rules, and reading-duration formulas.
lessons.example: Adjusting tracking on a fast-flashing lower third to ensure viewers can absorb 6 words within a 2.5-second on-screen window.

lessons.lesson_title: Asset Engineering: Illustrator Layer Separation & Photoshop Cutouts
lessons.what_is_taught: Preparing motion-ready vector assets and raster elements for After Effects animation. Adobe Illustrator layer separation hygiene: organizing every animated element onto distinct top-level layers, descriptive naming conventions (e.g. L_Arm, R_Arm, Cog_Inner), removing stray anchor points, releasing clipping masks, expanding strokes, and centering anchor points. Adobe Photoshop cutouts: subject isolation using Select Subject and Pen Tool, mask preparation, cleaning hair/fringe with Refine Edge, content-aware inpainting for background plates, and multi-plane asset slicing to engineer parallax assets.
subtopics: Motion-ready vector assets: preparing complex branding artwork for clean After Effects import
Illustrator layer separation protocol: top-level layers vs sublayers, naming standards, and grouping rules
Vector cleanup: flattening appearances, expanding strokes, releasing clipping masks, and anchor point alignment
Photoshop cutouts and mask preparation: precision Pen Tool paths, Refine Edge hair masking, and clean alpha channels
Parallax assets preparation: reconstructing plates with Generative Fill and slicing depth planes for 2.5D environments
lessons.why_it_matters: Improperly layered or named files waste hours of studio time and break when imported into After Effects.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes a complex brand illustration, executes Illustrator layer separation across 15+ named layers, produces Photoshop cutouts with mask preparation, and slices parallax assets.
lessons.expected_outcome: A production-ready Illustrator file and Photoshop multi-layer PSD completely prepared for direct After Effects animation.
lessons.example: Separating a flat corporate character illustration into torso, limbs, and facial features so each can be independently rigged in After Effects.

lessons.lesson_title: Style Frames, Storyboarding & Motion Design Boards
lessons.what_is_taught: The pre-visualization pipeline in commercial motion design: translating a creative brief and script into visual concepts. Creating 3-to-5 key style frames in Photoshop and Illustrator that define the final visual look, color palette, lighting, texture, and typography. Storyboarding for motion graphics: sketching shot sequences, framing, pacing, and visual transitions. Constructing motion design boards showing transition mechanics, directional arrows, easing annotations, and animation cues for client sign-off.
subtopics: From creative brief to visual narrative: moodboards, aesthetic direction, and concept sketching
Crafting high-fidelity style frames: lighting, textural depth, typography, and graphic elements
Storyboarding for motion: framing, pacing, aspect ratio planning, and shot transition logic
Motion design boards: annotating motion cues, camera moves, timing notes, and transition paths across frames
Client pitching and feedback incorporation: securing visual approval to prevent costly revisions during animation
lessons.why_it_matters: Style frames guarantee client alignment on aesthetics before animation begins, eliminating painful complete rebuilds.
lessons.what_learner_does: Develops a 4-frame style board, detailed storyboarding sequence, and annotated motion design boards for a commercial fintech product launch.
lessons.expected_outcome: A 4-frame presentation-ready motion design board with style frames, color palette, typographic specs, and transition annotations.
lessons.example: Creating style frames for a fintech startup showing dark mode aesthetics, neon green financial charts, and clean typography.

modules.expected_outcome: Production-ready vector and photographic assets and approved style frames that directly feed into After Effects animation production.
modules.assessment_criteria: Asset separation hygiene & naming conventions (35%), Typographic hierarchy & layout systems (35%), Grid composition & style frame polish (30%).

modules.module_purpose: Master the technical core of the After Effects workspace (After Effects 26.5): compositions and timelines, layer types, transform properties (position, rotation, scale, opacity, anchor points), keyframes, parenting, null objects, pre-compositions, Graph Editor, speed and value graphs, custom easing, shape layers, paths, Trim Paths, Repeaters, path animation, text animators, range selectors, typography animation, masks, track mattes, blend modes, adjustment layers, motion blur, effects, basic expressions, Essential Properties, reusable compositions, render queue, Media Encoder integration, and professional project organization.

Manage all layer types: Solids, Adjustments, Null objects, Shape layers, Text, and Pre-compositions.
Animate transform properties: position, rotation, scale, opacity, and anchor points with precision keyframes.
Master the Graph Editor: sculpt speed and value graphs to execute custom easing, anticipation, and overshoot.
Build vector graphics with shape layers, paths, path animation, Trim Paths, Repeaters, and Merge Paths.
Construct kinetic typography animation using text animators, per-character 3D, and range selectors.
Deploy masks, track mattes (Alpha and Luma), blend modes, adjustment layers, motion blur, and effects.
Implement basic expressions (time, wiggle(), loopOut()), Essential Properties, and reusable compositions.

Layer Types & Transform Properties (Position, Rotation, Scale, Opacity)
Keyframes, Anchor Points, Parenting & Null Objects
Graph Editor, Speed and Value Graphs & Custom Easing
Shape Layers, Paths, Trim Paths, Repeaters & Path Animation

lessons.lesson_title: After Effects Workspace, Compositions and Timelines & Transform Properties
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the After Effects workspace (v26.5): configuring panels (Project, Timeline, Composition Viewer, Effects & Presets, Info). Setting up compositions and timelines: frame size (1920x1080, 1080x1920, 3840x2160), pixel aspect ratios (square 1.0), frame rates (24, 29.97, 60fps), and timecode formatting. Working with fundamental layer types: Solids, Null objects, Adjustment layers, Shape layers, and Text layers. Animating transform properties: position, rotation, scale, opacity, and anchor points. Setting keyframes, navigating the timeline with shortcuts, understanding spatial vs temporal interpolation, and using parenting and null objects to build animation rigs.
subtopics: After Effects workspace optimization: panel docking, workspace resets, cache settings, and shortcut keys
Compositions and timelines configuration: frame rates, square pixels, duration tokens, and resolution downsampling
Layer types taxonomy: Solids, Adjustment layers, Null objects, Shape layers, Text layers, and Pre-compositions
Transform properties deep dive: animating position, rotation, scale, opacity, and anchor points with precision keyframes
Parenting and null objects: building hierarchical controller rigs and establishing layer parent-child relationships
Project organization: structuring folders for footage, solids, audio, comps, and pre-rendered assets
lessons.why_it_matters: Anchor point misplacement and spatial interpolation drift are the two most common reasons beginner animations look sloppy and disjointed.
lessons.what_learner_does: Sets up a master 1080p composition, configures compositions and timelines, animates transform properties with parenting and null objects, and establishes project organization.
lessons.expected_outcome: A cleanly keyframed transform choreography project with correctly centered anchor points and deliberate spatial trajectories.
lessons.example: Animating an icon rotating from its geometric base rather than center by adjusting its anchor point with the Pan Behind tool.

lessons.lesson_title: The Graph Editor: Speed and Value Graphs & Custom Easing
lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the Graph Editor: moving beyond linear keyframes and basic Easy Ease (F9). Differentiating speed and value graphs: reading rate of change over time versus velocity in pixels per second. Sculpting speed curves: steep acceleration curves, long deceleration tails, snap-in-place custom easing, and anticipation dips. Simulating organic physical properties: inertia, mass, gravity, rebound, and overshoot. Enabling and configuring motion blur: shutter angle, samples per frame, and GPU acceleration for hyper-fluid motion physics.
subtopics: The Graph Editor interface: navigating and toggling between speed and value graphs for all transform properties
Speed and value graphs analysis: reading velocity peaks, zero-points, and acceleration slopes
Custom easing curves: manipulating Bezier handles to achieve snappy commercial easing (75%-85% influence)
Physics simulation: crafting anticipation wind-ups, velocity bursts, and overshoot-and-settle curves
Motion blur configuration: adjusting shutter angle (180° vs 360°) and motion blur samples for fluid realism
lessons.why_it_matters: Linear and generic Easy-Ease animations look amateurish; professional motion design quality is judged almost entirely by Graph Editor speed curve mastery.
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates a series of mechanical and organic objects, sculpting speed and value graphs with custom easing and enabling motion blur.
lessons.expected_outcome: A speed-graph exercise comp displaying three distinct easing styles: punchy commercial snap, smooth luxury deceleration, and bouncy cartoon physics.
lessons.example: Crafting a UI card reveal where the card rockets upward at 2000 px/sec and gently decelerates over 15 frames with an 85% influence speed curve.

lessons.lesson_title: Shape Layers, Paths, Trim Paths, Repeaters & Path Animation
lessons.what_is_taught: Vector shape layers architecture in After Effects: Shape Groups, paths, strokes, fills, and transform properties. Creating and animating bezier paths, path animation, convert vertex tool, and direction handles. Shape modifiers: Trim Paths (Start, End, Offset, simultaneously vs individually) for dynamic stroke reveals and charging bars. Repeaters for radial bursts, concentric rings, and patterned grid arrays. Merge Paths (Add, Subtract, Intersect, Exclude) for procedural shape cutting. Wiggle Paths and Zig Zag for procedural micro-movement. Linking shape layers to null objects.
subtopics: Shape layers internal hierarchy: Contents, Groups, paths, strokes, fills, and group transforms
Path animation: keyframing vector path vertices to deform shapes and animate geometric silhouettes
Trim Paths: animating Start, End, and Offset to build dynamic line art reveals, circuit traces, and progress rings
Repeaters: configuring copies, offset, position offsets, rotational fan arrays, and radial graphic bursts
Shape modifiers and effects: Merge Paths, Wiggle Paths, Round Corners, and Zig Zag procedural modifiers
lessons.why_it_matters: Shape layers scale infinitely without raster degradation and provide the primary building blocks for modern 2D animation, UI mockups, and logo reveals.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs an animated tech-HUD graphic featuring animated paths, Trim Paths line reveals, path animation, and radial repeater bursts parented to a central null.
lessons.expected_outcome: An infinite-resolution vector shape animation comp featuring coordinated Trim Paths, Repeaters, path animation, and null parenting.
lessons.example: Creating an animated checkmark reveal inside a pulsing circular boundary using Trim Paths and a secondary burst repeater.

lessons.lesson_title: Text Animators, Range Selectors & Typography Animation
lessons.what_is_taught: The After Effects text engine: point text vs paragraph text, font baselines, and typography animation. Adding text animators for Position, Scale, Rotation, Opacity, Tracking, Blur, and Character Offset. Mastering range selectors: Start, End, and Offset parameters. Advanced range selectors parameters: Units (Percentage vs Index), Based On (Characters, Characters Excluding Spaces, Words, Lines), Mode (Add, Subtract, Intersect), and Shape (Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Triangle, Round, Smooth). Customizing Ease High and Ease Low for per-character typographic motion curves. Enabling per-character 3D for dimensional text tumbling.
subtopics: Typography animation fundamentals: font kerning preservation, tracking, and motion legibility standards
Text animators engine: combining Position, Scale, Tracking, Opacity, and Blur animators on a single text layer
Range selectors mechanics: animating Start, End, and Offset to create sequential character and word cascades
Advanced selector shapes: Ramp Up, Ramp Down, and Smooth selector curves for organic letter ripples
Per-character 3D: enabling dimensional text rotation and spatial z-depth reveals
lessons.why_it_matters: Kinetic typography is demanded in nearly every commercial video; range selectors provide scalable letter-by-letter animation without manual keyframing.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds three distinct typography animation presets using text animators and range selectors: punchy word reveals, cascading blur reveals, and expanding tracked headers.
lessons.expected_outcome: A kinetic typography showcase comp demonstrating per-character range selector control with custom ease curves.
lessons.example: Creating a title sequence where each letter falls from above with a 20px blur, landing with an organic spring settle using Ramp Up selector shape.

lessons.lesson_title: Masks, Track Mattes, Expressions, Essential Properties & Render Output
lessons.what_is_taught: Compositing workflows in After Effects: Pen Tool vector masks, feathering, expansion, and animated mask paths. Track mattes: Alpha Matte, Alpha Inverted Matte, Luma Matte, and Luma Inverted Matte. Blend modes (Screen, Multiply, Overlay, Add) and adjustment layers for global color treatments. Pre-compositions and reusable compositions architecture. Basic expressions: time*, wiggle(frequency, amplitude), and loopOut('cycle'). Essential Properties: exposing text, colors, and sliders for reusable compositions. Output pipelines: render queue (ProRes 422, ProRes 4444 with RGB+Alpha), Media Encoder integration (H.264/H.265), effects application, and project organization.
subtopics: Masks and feathering: creating animated vector masks, mask expansion, and inverted cutouts
Track mattes mastery: deploying Alpha and Luma track mattes for graphic framing and complex reveals
Pre-compositions and reusable compositions: nesting comp hierarchies, collapse transformations, and clean naming
Effects and adjustment layers: applying blurs, glow, color balance, and distortion globally
Basic expressions: time*, wiggle(freq, amp), and loopOut('cycle') for procedural continuous animation
Essential Properties: exposing text, colors, and slider controls to build versatile reusable compositions
Render queue and Media Encoder integration: exporting ProRes masters with alpha and compressed MP4 deliverables
Project organization and archiving: Collect Files routines and missing footage resolution
lessons.why_it_matters: Reusable templates, efficient pre-comps, and proper alpha channel exports form the operational backbone of professional agency motion delivery.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a lower-third template utilizing masks, track mattes, pre-compositions, basic expressions, and Essential Properties, exporting via render queue and Media Encoder integration.
lessons.expected_outcome: A complete, modular lower-third asset with Essential Properties enabled and tested across different text lengths, with verified alpha transparency.
lessons.example: Setting up a broadcast lower third where editors can change the name, title, and bar color directly in Essential Properties without opening the pre-comp.

modules.business_application: Foundational After Effects competencies required for full-time motion designer, animator, and video editor roles across advertising agencies, broadcast channels, and digital studios.
modules.expected_outcome: A versatile set of reusable broadcast-quality motion graphics assets built with robust pre-comps, custom Graph Editor physics, and export compliance.

modules.module_purpose: Synthesize motion design fundamentals into polished creative deliverables: animated logo reveal and stings, kinetic typography and text transitions, shape transitions, lower thirds, callouts, social graphics, and animation loops with beat synchronization, smooth easing, overshoot and follow-through, motion consistency, alpha channel export, and template reusability.
what_you_will_learn: Produce polished commercial animated logo reveal stings utilizing shape reveals, vector write-ons, and dynamic settle physics.

Template structure and master controller nulls: organizing parametric animation rigs

Integrating tracked typography: embedding 3D text layers and motion graphics into live-action physical spaces. Perspective matching and parallax: creating realistic multi-depth separation between foreground, subject, and background text as the camera traverses the scene.
subtopics: 3D Camera Tracker architecture: solving camera focal length, sensor size, and optical distortion
Track quality checks: reviewing point cloud density and achieving camera solve error below 1.0 pixel
Establishing world coordinates: setting ground planes, origin points, and coordinate orientation
Tracked typography integration: anchoring 3D text and HUD graphics into live-action physical spaces
Parallax dynamics: verifying proper spatial depth and camera-perspective movement between near and far objects
Motion-tracking troubleshooting: addressing rolling shutter distortion, sudden camera whips, and feature dropouts
lessons.why_it_matters: 3D Camera tracking enables the illusion that computer graphics physically exist in the real world, obeying natural perspective, scale, and parallax depth.
lessons.what_learner_does: Runs the 3D Camera Tracker on aerial drone footage, achieves an average error under 0.8 pixels, sets a ground plane, and composites floating 3D tracked typography with natural parallax.
lessons.expected_outcome: A cinematic 3D camera-tracked shot with tracked typography seamlessly anchored to a physical landscape with authentic camera parallax.
lessons.example: Placing giant dimensional 3D letters behind a mountain range in drone footage, allowing the camera to pass by with realistic perspective shifts.

modules.hands_on_practice: Produce a camera-tracked shot with a realistic screen replacement and integrated text/graphics.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: A complete tracking and camera integration submission (.aep) containing (1) a photorealistic smartphone or laptop screen replacement with corner pinning, reflection matching, and occlusion handling in Mocha AE, and (2) a 3D camera-tracked landscape shot with tracked typography anchored to the ground plane demonstrating perspective matching, parallax, and solve error < 1.0 pixel.
modules.business_application: Commercial VFX, mobile app advertising, tech product commercials, and corporate explainer videos requiring realistic screen insertions and motion-tracked graphics.
modules.expected_outcome: Two production-quality camera-tracked shots exhibiting zero drift, realistic perspective matching, screen reflections, and clean parallax depth.
modules.assessment_criteria: Track stability & zero drift (40%), Screen lighting & reflection realism (30%), 3D camera solve error (<1.0px) & perspective matching (30%).

modules.module_purpose: Master professional subject isolation, rotoscoping workflow, and compositing: manual masking, rotoscoping workflow, Roto Brush or current supported equivalent (Roto Brush 3.0), Refine Edge, AI Object Matte, mask tracking, green-screen keying, spill suppression, alpha channels, premultiplication, edge feathering, colour matching, grain matching, edge blending, object removal, object cleanup, multi-layer compositing, AI matte artifact correction, and realism checks.
what_you_will_learn: Isolate moving subjects using manual masking and articulated rotoscoping workflow.
Deploy Roto Brush or current supported equivalent (Roto Brush 3.0) and AI Object Matte for accelerated subject propagation.
Master Refine Edge tools to preserve hair, fur, transparent fabric, and fine motion detail.
Execute mask tracking and combine garbage mattes with procedural isolation mattes.
Perform professional green-screen keying and advanced spill suppression using Keylight.
Understand alpha channels, premultiplication (straight vs premultiplied), and edge feathering.
Execute seamless colour matching, grain matching, edge blending, and AI matte artifact correction.
Execute object removal, object cleanup, multi-layer compositing, and comprehensive realism checks.
key_concepts: Roto Brush 3.0, Refine Edge & AI Object Matte
Object Removal, Object Cleanup & Realism Checks
modules.ai_integration: Leveraging Roto Brush 3.0 deep-learning model propagation and AI Object Matte algorithms for rapid initial segmentation, paired with rigorous manual spline correction, edge freeze caching, and AI matte artifact correction.

lessons.lesson_title: Rotoscoping Workflow: Manual Masking, Roto Brush & AI Object Matte
lessons.what_is_taught: The science and craft of rotoscoping: articulated rotoscoping workflow breaking human bodies into separate shapes (head, torso, limbs) to avoid boiling edges. Manual masking using Pen Tool beziers and mask tracking with Mocha AE. Deploying Roto Brush or current supported equivalent (Roto Brush 3.0): setting base frames, propagating forward/backward, and painting corrective strokes. Refine Edge tool: capturing hair, fur, sheer fabric, motion blur, and decontamination. Working with AI Object Matte in AE 26.5: disk caching propagation data to prevent playback slowdowns. AI matte artifact correction: repairing edge chatter, boundary hopping, and temporal flicker.
subtopics: Rotoscoping workflow: articulated shape breakdown (head, limbs, torso) to prevent boiling edges
Manual masking and mask tracking: keyframing bezier splines and tracking masks with Mocha AE
Roto Brush or current supported equivalent: base frames, propagation directions, and corrective strokes
Refine Edge tool: capturing hair strands, semi-transparent edges, motion blur, and edge decontamination
AI Object Matte in AE 26.5: disk caching propagation data to prevent playback slowdowns
AI matte artifact correction: fixing edge chatter, temporal flickering, and false-boundary detections
lessons.why_it_matters: Clean subject isolation without green screen is an essential VFX competency; sloppy rotoscoping with edge chatter instantly breaks production value.
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates an actor from a complex city background using Roto Brush 3.0 and Refine Edge, performs AI matte artifact correction, and freezes the propagation.
lessons.expected_outcome: A perfectly isolated subject matte preserving fine hair strands with zero edge chatter or temporal flickering.
lessons.example: Rotoscoping an athlete running across an urban street to sandwich animated brand typography behind them.

lessons.lesson_title: Green-Screen Keying, Spill Suppression & Alpha Channels
lessons.what_is_taught: Professional chroma keying using Keylight in After Effects: selecting screen colour, balancing screen pre-blur, and setting screen balance. Inspecting Screen Matte view: clipping blacks, clipping whites, and eliminating transparency holes in core subjects. Spill suppression: neutralizing green spill on hair, skin, and wardrobe without desaturating natural flesh tones. Understanding alpha channels and premultiplication: differentiating Straight Alpha vs Premultiplied Alpha in composite stacks to eliminate dark edge fringing. Applying edge feathering, choked mattes, and edge blending using light wrap techniques.
subtopics: Green-screen keying with Keylight: Screen Colour selection, Screen Pre-blur, and Screen Balance
Screen Matte inspection: checking clip black, clip white, and transparency holes in status view
Spill suppression: neutralizing green spill on hair and clothing without shifting natural flesh tones
Alpha channels and premultiplication: differentiating Straight Alpha vs Premultiplied Alpha in composite stacks
Edge feathering and edge blending: choked mattes, light wrap effects, and luminance blending
Edge cleanup: combining garbage mattes and core mattes to preserve delicate hair details
lessons.why_it_matters: Poor chroma keying leads to green fringes, hollow transparent bodies, and unnatural cutout looks; professional keying and spill suppression make synthetic backgrounds look authentic.
lessons.what_learner_does: Keys an actor shot against green screen, eliminates green spill with spill suppression, applies light wrap edge blending, and inspects alpha channels.
lessons.expected_outcome: A clean chroma key composite with natural hair detail, zero green spill, and seamless edge blending into a new background.
lessons.example: Keying a presenter in a studio and compositing them into a sleek virtual control room with ambient edge wrap.

lessons.lesson_title: Object Removal, Multi-Layer Compositing & Realism Checks
lessons.what_is_taught: Plate cleanup and invisible visual effects: object removal and object cleanup to erase boom mics, tracking markers, logos, and wires from moving shots. Clean-plating workflows: freeze frames, Photoshop Generative Fill patches, and Mocha planar tracking. Multi-layer compositing: assembling complex composite stacks with foreground subjects, midground elements, and background plates. Colour matching: balancing black levels, midtone gamma, and highlight color temperatures across disparately lit elements. Grain matching: sampling sensor noise from source footage and applying matched grain to synthetic layers. Comprehensive realism checks: evaluating shadow direction, specular reflections, motion blur match, and optical edge bleed.
subtopics: Object removal and object cleanup: removing boom mics, tracking markers, logos, and wires from moving shots
Clean-plating workflows: freeze frames, Photoshop Generative Fill patches, and Mocha planar tracking
Multi-layer compositing: sandwiching graphics, backgrounds, and subjects with proper depth planes
Colour matching: harmonizing black levels, midtone gamma, and highlight color temperature across layers
Grain matching: sampling sensor noise from source footage and applying matched grain to synthetic layers
Realism checks: evaluating shadow direction, specular reflections, motion blur match, and optical edge bleed
lessons.why_it_matters: Invisible VFX and cleanup comprise the majority of commercial post-production; colour matching, grain matching, and realism checks ensure seamless integration.
lessons.what_learner_does: Executes object removal to erase unwanted equipment, color-matches a composite to source footage, applies matched camera grain, and runs realism checks.
lessons.expected_outcome: A multi-layer composite with object cleanup, matched color and grain, and a before/after split screen demonstrating invisible integration.
lessons.example: Removing safety wires from an actor performing a stunt and matching the camera's ISO 1600 sensor noise across the repaired patch.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create a clean subject-isolation and background-replacement composite, with before/after breakdown.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: A complete rotoscoping and compositing project package (.aep) containing (1) an actor isolated from a complex background using Roto Brush 3.0 / AI Object Matte with hair-level Refine Edge, (2) an object removal and cleanup sequence using clean plates, (3) a green-screen keying composite with spill suppression and light wrap, and (4) a before/after split-screen breakdown showing edge blending, colour matching, and grain matching passing all realism checks.
modules.business_application: Commercial post-production, VFX feature pipelines, music videos, and corporate advertising requiring seamless subject extraction, plate replacement, and cleanup.
modules.expected_outcome: A broadcast-ready multi-layer composite with hair-level edge refinement, zero matte chatter, matched color/grain, and an informative before/after breakdown.
modules.assessment_criteria: Edge stability & lack of edge chatter (40%), Hair detail preservation & spill suppression (30%), Colour matching, grain matching & realism checks (30%).

modules.module_purpose: Elevate visual effects production into photoreal cinematic environments: camera layers, 2.5D environments, lighting, depth of field, parallax, shadows, reflections, atmospheric effects, particles, scene interaction, AI-generated plate integration, perspective matching, compositing realism, and scene continuity.
what_you_will_learn: Construct 2.5D environments using camera layers and multi-plane depth distribution.
Configure physical camera simulation: optical focal lengths, depth of field, and aperture iris blades.
Simulate realistic lighting: directional lights, ambient bounce, point lights, and falloff curves.
Generate realistic contact shadows, cast shadows, and environmental reflections.
Create atmospheric effects: haze, fog, dust motes, and particle systems.
Integrate AI-generated plate integration and digital matte paintings with perspective matching.
Establish natural scene interaction between synthetic elements and live-action foregrounds.
Maintain rigorous compositing realism and scene continuity across sequential shots.
modules.ai_integration: Employing generative AI models (Adobe Firefly / Midjourney) for generating background matte painting plates and atmospheric texture elements, while executing all 3D camera staging, lighting setups, perspective matching, and shadow projection manually.

lessons.lesson_title: 2.5D Environments, Camera Layers & Depth of Field
lessons.what_is_taught: Building dimensional multi-plane 2.5D environments in After Effects: slicing graphic, photographic, and matte-painted plates across 3D Z-depth space. Camera layers configuration: choosing 35mm vs 50mm vs 85mm optical lenses and field of view calibration. Parallax dynamics: distributing layers to achieve natural depth separation as the virtual camera dollies and pans. Depth of field optics: animating Focus Distance, Aperture, and Blur Level for cinematic shallow focus and bokeh. AI-generated plate integration: matching horizon lines, vanishing points, and lens distortion of AI-generated matte painting backgrounds to live-action foreground plates.
subtopics: 2.5D environments architecture: slicing background, midground, and foreground assets into 3D camera space
Camera layers setup: choosing 35mm vs 50mm vs 85mm optical lenses and field of view calibration
Parallax and depth distribution: positioning layers in Z-space to achieve natural depth separation during camera moves
Depth of field configuration: animating Focus Distance, Aperture, and Blur Level for cinematic shallow focus
AI-generated plate integration: matching horizon lines, vanishing points, and lens distortion of AI background plates
Perspective matching: aligning virtual camera coordinates to physical plate geometry
lessons.why_it_matters: 2.5D environments allow editors and motion designers to create sweeping cinematic camera moves through static artwork and matte paintings.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a multi-plane 2.5D environment using camera layers, integrates an AI-generated matte painting plate with perspective matching, and animates a cinematic camera move with depth of field.
lessons.expected_outcome: A dimensional 2.5D environment sequence with organic parallax, optical depth of field, and seamless plate integration.
lessons.example: Transforming a 2D fantasy landscape into an immersive 3D scene where the camera flies past foreground trees toward a distant castle.

lessons.lesson_title: Lighting, Shadows, Atmospheric Effects & Compositing Realism
lessons.what_is_taught: Lighting simulation in composite scenes: setting key lights, fill lights, ambient lights, and inverse-square falloff curves. Shadows engineering: configuring Cast Shadows, Shadow Darkness, and Shadow Diffusion to ground synthetic objects onto physical floors. Surface reflections: building environmental floor and table reflections using blurred inverted duplicate layers with opacity falloff. Atmospheric effects and particles: introducing volumetric fog, light rays, dust motes, and particle systems to create atmospheric perspective. Scene interaction and scene continuity: ensuring light direction, color temperature, and contrast match across sequential shots. Compositing realism audits: eliminating floating elements, synthetic black-point mismatches, and unreal edge sharpness.
subtopics: Lighting simulation: directional key lights, fill lights, ambient lights, and inverse-square falloff
Shadows engineering: configuring Cast Shadows, Shadow Darkness, and Shadow Diffusion for contact grounding
Reflections: building ground and table reflections using blurred inverted duplicate layers with falloff
Atmospheric effects and particles: adding subtle dust motes, floating embers, volumetric light rays, and smoke
Scene interaction: simulating light spill and color bounce between composite layers and live-action elements
Compositing realism and scene continuity: auditing light angles, black levels, and optical characteristics across sequential shots
lessons.why_it_matters: Shadows, reflections, and atmospheric particles provide the essential subconscious cues that convince the human eye a composite scene is physically real.
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds realistic directional lighting, contact shadows, floor reflections, and atmospheric particles to a synthetic element, auditing compositing realism.
lessons.expected_outcome: A photorealistic commercial VFX composition with grounded shadows, convincing reflections, atmospheric particles, and perfect scene continuity.
lessons.example: Compositing a synthetic sports car onto a live-action asphalt road with realistic tire contact shadows, headlights casting volumetric fog, and wet road reflections.

modules.hands_on_practice: Produce one commercial VFX composition with convincing environment integration.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: A complete commercial VFX composition (.aep) featuring a 2.5D environment built from camera layers, AI-generated plate integration, matched perspective and depth of field, realistic cast shadows and reflections, atmospheric effects or particles, and flawless compositing realism.
modules.business_application: High-end television commercials, music videos, cinematic titles, and digital advertisements requiring photorealistic environment extensions and visual enhancements.
modules.expected_outcome: A 10–15-second commercial VFX shot featuring believable environmental depth, physical lighting, cast shadows, and atmospheric integration.
modules.assessment_criteria: Lighting, shadow & reflection realism (35%), Depth of field, parallax & perspective matching (35%), Plate integration, atmospheric effects & scene continuity (30%).

modules.module_purpose: Introduce fundamental 3D workflows for motion designers using Blender: Blender interface, object primitives, basic modeling, materials, lighting, camera setup, product rotation, keyframe animation, transparent-background renders, render passes, export formats, compositing 3D renders in After Effects, and basic render troubleshooting (without over-promising advanced 3D modeling, character rigging, or Hollywood CGI mastery).
what_you_will_learn: Navigate the Blender interface, 3D viewport, outliner, and properties panels.
Create and manipulate object primitives: translate, rotate, scale, and apply basic modeling modifiers (Bevel, Subsurf).
Apply materials: configure Principled BSDF shader for roughness, metallic sheen, and base color.
Configure 3-point lighting setups and camera setup for commercial product rendering.
Animate product rotation and transform keyframe animation on the timeline.
Render image sequences with transparent-background renders (RGBA) in Cycles and Eevee.
Understand render passes (Combined, Shadow, Ambient Occlusion, Cryptomatte) and export formats (PNG 16-bit, OpenEXR).
Composite 3D renders into After Effects with color grading, shadows, and basic render troubleshooting.
key_concepts: Compositing 3D Renders in After Effects & Basic Render Troubleshooting
modules.ai_integration: Utilizing AI text-to-texture generation tools for rapid material texture ideation, combined with fundamental manual 3D modeling, lighting, and timeline keyframing.

lessons.lesson_title: Blender Interface, Basic Modeling & Material Shading
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the Blender interface: 3D Viewport navigation, Outliner hierarchy, Properties panel, and essential transformation hotkeys (G, R, S, X/Y/Z constraints). Working with object primitives: adding cubes, cylinders, spheres, and empties. Basic modeling techniques: extruding, insetting, edge loop cuts, and applying non-destructive modifiers (Bevel modifier for rounded edges, Subdivision Surface modifier for smooth geometry). Shading and materials: configuring the Principled BSDF shader (Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Normal mapping). Setting up studio lighting: 3-point lighting (Key light, Fill light, Rim light) and HDRI environment illumination.
subtopics: Blender interface navigation: 3D Viewport, Outliner, Properties, Shading workspaces, and essential hotkeys (G, R, S, X/Y/Z)
Object primitives: adding cubes, cylinders, spheres, and empties; applying scale and transform origins
Basic modeling techniques: extruding, insetting, edge loops, and non-destructive modifiers (Bevel, Subdivision Surface)
Materials and shaders: configuring the Principled BSDF shader (Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Normal mapping)
Lighting setup: 3-point studio lighting (Key, Fill, Rim) and HDRI world background illumination
Camera setup: focal length, sensor fit, depth of field, and framing product assets
lessons.why_it_matters: A working knowledge of Blender enables motion designers to create custom 3D packshots and product assets without depending on stock 3D models.
lessons.what_learner_does: Navigates Blender, models a sleek tech product packaging element from object primitives, applies realistic materials, and configures studio lighting.
lessons.expected_outcome: A cleanly modeled and shaded 3D product asset illuminated with a commercial 3-point lighting setup.
lessons.example: Modeling a cosmetic serum bottle with a glass material, metallic cap, and paper label illuminated under soft studio rim lights.

lessons.lesson_title: Animation, Rendering & Compositing in After Effects
lessons.what_is_taught: Camera setup and timeline keyframe animation in Blender: animating product rotation around a 360-degree turntable axis with smooth interpolation. Rendering engines: Eevee Next vs Cycles. Transparent-background renders: enabling Film > Transparent to output clean RGBA alpha channels. Understanding render passes (Combined, Diffuse, Glossy, Shadow Catcher, Ambient Occlusion) and export formats (16-bit PNG image sequences vs OpenEXR multi-layer). Compositing 3D renders in After Effects: importing image sequences, matching motion blur, shadow catchers, and color grading. Basic render troubleshooting: fixing inverted normals, texture path breaks, clipping limits, and sampling noise.
subtopics: Camera setup: setting focal length, clipping limits, sensor presets, and framing product shots
Product rotation animation: setting timeline keyframes for smooth 360-degree turntable product rotations
Keyframe animation curves: fine-tuning interpolation in the Blender Graph Editor
Transparent-background renders: enabling Film > Transparent in Cycles/Eevee for clean RGBA alpha output
Render passes and export formats: outputting PNG 16-bit RGBA sequences and understanding OpenEXR passes
Compositing 3D renders in After Effects: importing image sequences, matching motion blur, shadow catchers, and color grade
Basic render troubleshooting: resolving flipped normals, clipping issues, missing textures, and sampling noise
lessons.why_it_matters: Knowing how to output transparent renders and composite 3D passes into After Effects completes the cross-software pipeline for modern commercial motion design.
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates a 360-degree product rotation, renders a transparent-background PNG sequence, composites the 3D element into After Effects, and troubleshoots render artifacts.
lessons.expected_outcome: A rendered 3D product animation composited cleanly into an After Effects timeline with shadow catching and color grading.
lessons.example: Rendering a rotating luxury watch on transparent alpha and compositing it over dynamic particle backgrounds with glowing typography in After Effects.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create one simple animated 3D product element and integrate it into a motion-compositing shot.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: A complete Month 5 project commercial sequence (10–15 seconds) containing (1) a 3D product element modeled, textured, and animated with product rotation in Blender, (2) exported transparent-background renders, and (3) a final After Effects composite combining the 3D element with camera tracking, background footage, shadows, and motion graphics.
modules.business_application: Commercial motion graphics, tech product commercials, e-commerce promotions, and agency social reels requiring sleek 3D product presentations composited into live-action footage.
modules.expected_outcome: A 10–15-second camera-tracked/VFX commercial sequence integrating an animated 3D product element with realistic lighting, shadows, and background interaction.
modules.assessment_criteria: 3D asset animation & clean alpha render (40%), After Effects compositing & lighting/color integration (35%), Shadow catching & render troubleshooting hygiene (25%).

modules.module_purpose: Master professional color science and grading in DaVinci Resolve: Resolve interface, Cut/Edit/Color workflows, primary colour correction (exposure, white balance, contrast), video scopes (waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope, histogram), node-based grading, shot matching, skin-tone correction, Power Windows, qualifiers, tracking, Rec.709, Log footage, LUTs, color management, colour-space transforms, cinematic looks, brand colour consistency, HDR/SDR awareness, and export colour integrity (with clear demarcation of free tools vs Studio-only neural features like IntelliSearch and CineFocus).
what_you_will_learn: Navigate the DaVinci Resolve interface across Cut/Edit/Color workflows and configure color management.
Execute primary colour correction: balance exposure, calibrate white balance, and sculpt tonal contrast.
Read and analyze video scopes: Waveform, RGB Parade, Vectorscope, and Histogram to ensure broadcast legality.
Build structured, modular node-based grading pipelines (serial, parallel, and layer nodes).
Execute precise shot matching across diverse camera angles and changing lighting conditions.
Perform skin-tone correction using the Vectorscope skin-tone line and secondary isolation tools.
Deploy Power Windows, qualifiers (HSL and 3D), and planar tracking to isolate and grade scene regions.
Ingest and normalize Log footage (Sony S-Log3, Canon C-Log, Apple Log) using colour-space transforms (CST) and LUTs.
Design cinematic looks while enforcing strict brand colour consistency and export colour integrity.
Understand HDR/SDR awareness and transparently evaluate free tools vs Studio-only features (IntelliSearch where available, CineFocus where supported).
key_concepts: Video Scopes (Waveform, RGB Parade, Vectorscope, Histogram)
Free vs Studio Feature Demarcation & Export Colour Integrity
modules.ai_integration: Exploring DaVinci Resolve Studio Neural Engine tools where available (IntelliSearch smart footage indexing, CineFocus depth-of-field tools, Face Refinement) while mastering universally applicable manual color grading pipelines available in free DaVinci Resolve.

lessons.lesson_title: DaVinci Resolve Interface, Video Scopes & Primary Colour Correction
lessons.what_is_taught: DaVinci Resolve interface navigation: Media, Cut, Edit, Color, and Deliver pages; Cut/Edit/Color workflows. Reading and interpreting video scopes: Waveform (evaluating luminance distribution), RGB Parade (analyzing color balance across red, green, and blue channels), Vectorscope (measuring hue and saturation), and Histogram. Primary colour correction: setting black points with Lift, balancing midtones with Gamma, and shaping peak highlights with Gain. Controlling exposure, white balance, and contrast using primary color wheels, temp/tint sliders, and custom curves. Enforcing broadcast legal signal ranges.
subtopics: Resolve interface navigation: Cut/Edit/Color workflows, media pool management, and viewer transport
Video scopes analysis: Waveform, RGB Parade, Vectorscope, and Histogram calibration
Primary colour correction: Lift, Gamma, Gain, and Offset tonal adjustments
Exposure, white balance, and contrast: neutral grey balancing and tonal curve sculpting
Broadcast legality: monitoring clip levels to prevent crushed blacks (<0 IRE) and blown highlights (>100 IRE)
lessons.why_it_matters: Primary color correction establishes the neutral baseline for all visual storytelling; uncalibrated footage leads to muddy shadows, clipped highlights, and disjointed edits.
lessons.what_learner_does: Calibrates the Resolve interface, reads video scopes, neutralizes color casts, and balances exposure and contrast on a raw multicam scene.
lessons.expected_outcome: A perfectly neutralized, exposure-balanced sequence conforming to broadcast legal limits on waveform and RGB parade scopes.
lessons.example: Correcting a tungsten-cast interior shot so white shirts appear neutral at 128 on the RGB Parade and skin tones fall naturally.

lessons.lesson_title: Node-Based Grading, Log Footage Normalization & Colour-Space Transforms
lessons.what_is_taught: Building robust node-based grading architectures: serial nodes, parallel nodes, layer mixer nodes, and compound node trees. Understanding Log footage: wide dynamic range, logarithmic gamma curves, and desaturated flat profiles (Sony S-Log3, Canon C-Log2, Apple Log). Professional color management: DaVinci YRGB vs DaVinci YRGB Color Managed (RCM) vs ACES. Deploying Colour-space transforms (CST): non-destructively mapping camera raw Log gamuts into standard Rec.709. Utilizing 3D LUTs: technical conversion LUTs vs creative look LUTs, avoiding clipping, and generating custom show LUTs (.cube).
subtopics: Node-based grading architecture: structuring serial, parallel, and layer mixer node pipelines
Log footage characteristics: wide dynamic range capture and flat logarithmic profiles
Color management systems: DaVinci YRGB Color Managed vs ACES color workflows
Colour-space transforms (CST): accurately converting camera Log gamuts into Rec.709 standard
LUTs application: technical normalization LUTs vs creative styling LUTs (.cube)
lessons.why_it_matters: Colour-space transforms preserve maximum dynamic range and color bit-depth far better than destructive one-click LUTs.
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a standardized 8-node grading tree, normalizes mixed Log footage using Colour-Space Transforms, and builds custom show LUTs.
lessons.expected_outcome: A standardized node tree template that normalizes multi-camera Log footage into a rich Rec.709 color space without clipped data.
lessons.example: Applying a CST node to convert 10-bit Sony S-Log3 footage into Rec.709, retaining delicate cloud detail in the highlights.

lessons.lesson_title: Secondary Grading: Power Windows, Qualifiers & Skin-Tone Correction
lessons.what_is_taught: Secondary color grading precision: isolating specific colors, saturations, and luminance levels using HSL and 3D Qualifiers. Power Windows: linear, circular, polygon, and curve windows for regional lighting adjustments. High-speed planar tracking in Resolve: locking Power Windows to moving faces, hands, and scene elements. Skin-tone correction: isolating actor skin tones, analyzing alignment along the Vectorscope skin-tone line across diverse ethnicities, and smoothing skin texture. Demarcation of free vs Studio-only Resolve features: understanding IntelliSearch where available and CineFocus where supported versus manual grading tools.
subtopics: Qualifiers mastery: isolating targeted colors using HSL and 3D Qualifiers with matte clean radius
Power Windows: shaping vignettes, spotlights, and regional correction masks
Tracking: planar tracking Power Windows to moving subjects through camera movement
Skin-tone correction: aligning hues along the Vectorscope skin-tone line across diverse ethnicities
Free vs Studio-only Resolve tools: evaluating IntelliSearch where available and CineFocus where supported vs manual grading equivalents
lessons.why_it_matters: Viewers immediately spot unnatural skin tones; secondary qualifiers and Power Windows allow colorists to sculpt lighting and protect human skin tones.
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates an actor's face with a circular Power Window, tracks it with the planar tracker, qualifies skin tones to align with the skin-tone line, and refines contrast.
lessons.expected_outcome: Flawlessly corrected, natural skin tones that remain locked to the subject across rapid camera movement.
lessons.example: Tracking a Power Window onto an actress walking through changing sunlight to keep her skin tones warm and consistent without altering the background.

lessons.lesson_title: Shot Matching, Cinematic Looks, Brand Colour Consistency & Export Integrity
lessons.what_is_taught: Executing seamless shot matching across an entire sequence: matching exposure, contrast, and color balance between A-cam and B-cam setups. Designing stylized cinematic looks: teal & orange split-toning, filmic warmth, bleach bypass, and analog grain emulation. Enforcing brand colour consistency: locking corporate hex/Pantone colors to ensure brand logos and product colors are not distorted by creative looks. HDR/SDR awareness: understanding high dynamic range color volume (Rec.2020) versus SDR Rec.709 delivery. Export colour integrity: resolving the QuickTime gamma shift bug (gamma 1.96 vs 2.4 vs 2.2), setting color space tags, and conducting final scope QA.
subtopics: Shot matching methodology: matching exposure, black levels, and skin tones across sequential camera angles
Cinematic looks: developing filmic palettes, split-toning, and aesthetic grain textures
Brand colour consistency: isolating and preserving exact corporate brand colors from global look grades
HDR/SDR awareness: color volume considerations, peak brightness limits, and mastering standards
Export colour integrity: calibrating QuickTime gamma tags (Rec.709-A) to ensure colors display identically across web, mobile, and broadcast monitors
lessons.why_it_matters: Inconsistent color between shots distracts viewers, while gamma shifts during export ruin days of grading work; export colour integrity ensures the client sees exactly what you graded.
lessons.what_learner_does: Shot-matches 6 sequential scenes from an interview, crafts an intentional cinematic look, protects brand colors, and renders master files with verified export colour integrity.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully graded 90-second cinematic scene featuring 6 matched multi-camera shots with consistent skin tones, intentional look, and verified export color tags.
lessons.example: Matching a close-up shot from an iPhone with a wide shot from an ARRI Alexa, applying a film print look, and ensuring the company's trademark cyan logo remains spot-on.

modules.hands_on_practice: Grade a multi-shot footage sequence with corrected exposure, consistent skin tones and intentional cinematic look.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: A fully graded multi-camera scene (.drp and ProRes master) containing at least 6 sequential shots from Log footage demonstrating (1) accurate colour-space transforms to Rec.709, (2) balanced exposure and contrast verified on scopes, (3) flawless shot matching between cameras, (4) skin-tone correction aligned with the Vectorscope indicator, (5) Power Windows with planar tracking, and (6) an intentional cinematic look with verified export colour integrity.

Brickwall limiting: setting True Peak ceiling (-1.0 dBFS) to eliminate digital clipping. Basic mixing architecture: routing tracks into Dialogue (DX), Sound Effects (FX), and Music (MX) sub-busses and balancing faders across the stereo field.

lessons.lesson_title: Mixed-Media Editorial Assembly, Continuity & Transition Design
lessons.what_is_taught: Editorial assembly of mixed-media commercial timelines: combining real footage and generated clips in Adobe Premiere Pro. Establishing mixed-media creative direction and enforcing real/AI shot continuity across frame rates, motion blur, and camera grain. Designing multi-clip transition design: using whip pans, light leaks, match-cuts, and object wipes to transition seamlessly between physical live-action shots and synthetic AI environments. Conforming AI clips (normalizing non-standard frame rates, color spaces, and aspect ratios). Structured project organization: bin taxonomy, label coloring, and proxy workflows for AI media.
subtopics: Combining real footage and generated clips: editorial strategies to bridge physical and synthetic media
Mixed-media creative direction: establishing visual rules that make hybrid aesthetics intentional and stylish
Real/AI shot continuity: matching motion blur shutter angle, camera velocity, and visual rhythm
Conforming generative media: converting variable frame rates and color gamuts into unified Premiere sequences
Multi-clip transition design: crafting whip pans, motion blur zooms, and match-cuts across footage boundaries
Project organization: structuring footage bins (01_REAL, 02_AI_GENERATED, 03_VOX, 04_MOGRT) and media caching
lessons.why_it_matters: A commercial featuring jarring, unmotivated cuts between real actors and AI environments looks amateurish; seamless mixed-media editing creates a unified cinematic world.
lessons.what_learner_does: Assembles a 30-second mixed-media timeline in Premiere Pro combining 4 live-action shots and 4 AI clips, designing custom match-cut transitions.
lessons.expected_outcome: A cohesive rough cut seamlessly interweaving live-action and AI video with consistent pacing and intentional transition design.
lessons.example: Cutting from a real actor looking up in an office to an AI-generated shot of a futuristic metropolis, bridged by an upward camera tilt match-cut.

lessons.what_is_taught: Advanced compositing in Adobe After Effects to unify hybrid shots: AI background extension, object replacement, and integrating AI-generated scene elements into live-action plates. Masking and rotoscoping (using Roto Brush and Mocha AE) to place live subjects into AI backgrounds. Technical harmonization: colour matching (stripping contrast from oversaturated AI clips and matching black/midtone/highlight balance to camera profiles), light and shadow matching (creating cast shadows and light wraps), and camera/perspective matching. Adding matching sensor noise and lens artifacts (chromatic aberration, optical distortion). DaVinci finishing where relevant.
subtopics: AI background extension: expanding narrow aspect ratios or set boundaries using generative plates
Object replacement and AI-generated scene elements: compositing synthetic products or creatures into live scenes
Masking and rotoscoping: isolating live actors to sandwich them between AI foreground and background elements
Colour matching: neutralizing baked-in AI saturation and matching black levels, gamma, and gain to live footage
Light and shadow matching: projecting realistic contact shadows, surface reflections, and ambient light wrap
Camera/perspective matching & optical grain: aligning vanishing points and adding uniform sensor noise
lessons.why_it_matters: Raw AI clips rarely match the lighting and sensor grain of physical cinema cameras; precision compositing and color matching make synthetic elements indistinguishable from reality.
lessons.what_learner_does: Composites an AI-generated environmental extension behind a rotoscoped live actor in After Effects, matches lighting and shadows, and adds optical grain.
lessons.expected_outcome: A photoreal hybrid composite shot where live subjects and AI environments share identical lighting vectors, grain structure, and depth.
lessons.example: Placing a live-action actor recorded against a studio wall into an AI-generated Martian research outpost with red ambient light wrap.

lessons.lesson_title: Voiceover Generation, Audio Sync & Motion Graphics Finishing
lessons.what_is_taught: Audio post-production and motion graphics integration for hybrid commercials: voiceover generation using ElevenLabs, voice cloning protocols, and dubbing fundamentals. Audio-video synchronization: aligning voice cadence to visual cuts and performing lip-sync review where synthetic talking heads are utilized. Motion graphics integration: superimposing animated brand typography, UI callouts, price cards, and responsive MOGRT lower thirds onto hybrid footage. Final timeline polish, failure recovery (re-cutting timing or patching glitches), and preparing master timelines for final color grading and export.
subtopics: Voiceover generation in ElevenLabs: dialing in stability, clarity, and style exaggeration for commercial delivery
Dubbing fundamentals and audio-video synchronization: timing spoken words to visual pauses and montage cuts
Lip-sync review: evaluating synthetic mouth movements and correcting phonetic misalignment
Motion graphics integration: applying branded lower thirds, animated callout badges, and logo stings
Failure recovery: fixing dropped frames, audio pops, and masking anomalies on the master timeline
Final finishing workflow: roundtripping between Premiere, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve for final output
lessons.why_it_matters: High-end commercial impact depends on the synergy of dynamic motion graphics, punchy sound design, and broadcast-quality voiceover; graphics tie disparate footage together.
lessons.what_learner_does: Generates an ElevenLabs voiceover track, synchronizes it to a hybrid edit, adds animated brand motion graphics, and conducts a final lip-sync review.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully finished 30–45 second hybrid commercial featuring balanced voiceover, integrated sound effects, and animated brand motion graphics.
lessons.example: Adding an authoritative AI-generated voiceover, subtle UI HUD graphics, and a brand logo sting to complete a futuristic tech commercial.

lessons.lesson_title: AI Output Review, Brand Accuracy & Realism Evaluation
lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic auditing of generative media for commercial brand deployment: realism evaluation across physical textures, eye reflections, and fabric behavior. Brand accuracy and product fidelity: ensuring commercial logos, trademarked colors, packaging dimensions, and industrial design are not compromised by generative hallucinations. Verifying shot-to-shot consistency across multi-scene campaigns: evaluating facial likeness, costume styling, and environmental continuity. Building an objective scoring rubric to approve, revise, or discard AI assets before client presentation.
subtopics: Realism evaluation: auditing anatomical correctness, physical lighting logic, and surface interactions
Brand accuracy and product fidelity: auditing logo integrity, packaging proportions, and corporate pantones
Shot-to-shot consistency checks: evaluating multi-scene character likeness and wardrobe continuity
Generative flaw categorization: classifying flaws into fatal brand errors vs easily repairable artifacts
Client review preparation: presenting AI-generated media to non-technical stakeholders with realistic expectations
lessons.why_it_matters: Deploying AI assets with distorted brand logos or hallucinated product features damages enterprise brand equity and leads to rejected client work.

lessons.lesson_title: Legal, Licensing, Ethics & Provenance: Consent & Disclosure
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the legal landscape of commercial generative video: copyright status of purely AI-generated media vs human-assisted compilations. Commercial licensing: evaluating commercial usage terms across Firefly, Runway, Google Flow, and stock media libraries. Content provenance and authenticity: understanding C2PA metadata, cryptographic watermarking, and AI disclosure requirements in advertising. Ethical imperatives: obtaining consent for synthetic likeness, voice cloning permission, and strict enforcement of no impersonation without authorization. Maintaining client confidentiality: preventing NDA leaks by disabling public model training on proprietary assets.
subtopics: Copyright and commercial licenses: legal ownership of AI outputs and human authorship thresholds
Content provenance and C2PA: embedding and reading cryptographic metadata to verify media authenticity
AI disclosure standards in advertising: FTC, EU AI Act, and ASCI regulatory compliance in commercial marketing
Consent for synthetic likeness and voice cloning permission: legal model releases and biometric authorization
No impersonation without authorization: strict prohibitions against deepfakes, celebrity clones, and unauthorized voices
Client confidentiality and enterprise data security: configuring opt-outs for training data collection
lessons.why_it_matters: Unlicensed AI generation, unauthorized voice cloning, or failure to disclose synthetic media creates catastrophic copyright and legal liability for agencies and brands.
lessons.what_learner_does: Drafts an AI production compliance package including client disclosure statement, voice cloning release, and C2PA provenance audit.
lessons.expected_outcome: A certified legal and ethical compliance package covering commercial licensing, synthetic likeness consent, and C2PA disclosure.

lessons.lesson_title: Commercial Operational Management: Budgeting, Logs & Handoff
lessons.what_is_taught: Operational management of commercial AI production: managing AI generation credits, tracking GPU compute, and establishing iteration budgeting to prevent massive cost overruns. Maintaining generation logs: recording prompt strings, seed numbers, model versions, reference assets, and parameter settings to ensure reproducible project organization. Clarifying source file ownership: raw generations, layered project files (.prproj, .aep), and final master deliverables. Formulating client handoff requirements: packaging master videos, licensing certificates, prompt documentation, and raw asset archives.
subtopics: AI generation credits and compute budgeting: tracking platform costs per shot and setting generation limits
Generation logs management: logging seeds, prompts, model versions, and settings for 100% reproducibility
Reproducible project organization: directory taxonomy separating raw generations, approved selects, and clean plates
Source file ownership and contractual IP boundaries: establishing what the client owns (deliverable vs prompt IP)
Client handoff requirements: delivering master renders, textless archives, font licenses, and AI generation ledgers
lessons.why_it_matters: Without structured generation logs and iteration budgeting, AI projects become unreproducible money pits where lost seeds make minor revisions impossible.
lessons.what_learner_does: Establishes an iteration budget, tracks generation credits across a 6-shot sequence, maintains a prompt/seed log, and compiles a client handoff archive.
lessons.expected_outcome: A comprehensive project operations ledger featuring generation logs, compute budgets, and a formal client handoff package.
lessons.example: Providing a client with a full CSV generation log linking each 4K video file to its exact prompt, seed, model version, and commercial license.

Brand motion design: crafting custom animated typography, title cards, and logo stings in After Effects
VFX integration: executing screen replacements, object cleanup, and multi-plane 2.5D camera moves
Justified AI-generated footage integration: generating and compositing complex visual assets with matching lighting and grain
Multi-layer compositing: assembling complex visual stacks with foreground subjects, background plates, and motion graphics
Rough cut assembly: merging all visual disciplines into a cohesive 45–60 second picture-locked timeline
lessons.why_it_matters: Synthesizing editing, motion design, VFX, and AI into a singular, polished timeline is the ultimate demonstration of an industry-ready video professional.

subtopics: Cinematic colour grading in DaVinci Resolve: CST normalization, shot matching, and creative look styling
Fairlight sound mixing: dialogue cleanup, Foley sound design, dynamic ducking, and -14 LUFS mastering
Client feedback management: translating client revision requests into actionable technical tasks
Revision simulation: executing client-requested adjustments (pacing tweaks, color trim, graphic text updates)
Delivery QA checklist: conducting exhaustive quality control for audio sync, illegal broadcast colors, and compression artifacts
Master packaging: preparing final ProRes masters, client review files, and project archival handoffs
lessons.why_it_matters: Mastery over client revisions, sound mixing, and color grading separates entry-level editors from trusted post-production supervisors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Grades the commercial in Resolve, mixes audio to -14 LUFS in Fairlight, executes simulated client revisions, and runs a comprehensive delivery QA.

Re-timing voiceovers, re-cutting music beds with seamless audio splices, and condensing motion graphic transitions. Subtitle-safe areas and CTA/safe zones: overlaying TikTok/Reels UI templates to protect text and logos
Export profiles and render optimization: configuring bitrates and NCLC color tags for flawless mobile playback
Version naming and asset packaging: building clean delivery folders (CLIENT_PROJECT_DELIVERY_V01) with master and cutdown assets
