learning_objectives: Navigate the YouTube Partner Program (YPP) requirements, creator account prerequisites, two-step verification security, linked AdSense accounts, and platform monetization policies.

Analyze the February 1, 2027 YPP threshold changes (8,000 watch hours or 20M Shorts views for ads/Premium; 3,000 watch hours or 3M Shorts views for fan-funding), distinguishing time-sensitive published policy from permanent facts.

Evaluate the 12 primary YouTube revenue streams: Watch-page ads, YouTube Premium, Shorts ad pool, Channel Memberships, Super Chat, Super Stickers, Super Thanks, YouTube Shopping, affiliate marketing, brand sponsorships, digital merchandise, and creator consulting.
Calculate and forecast creator unit economics: CPM vs RPM, production overhead, software subscriptions, equipment depreciation, gross vs net creator margins, and break-even thresholds.
Structure transparent affiliate marketing funnels and YouTube Shopping integrations complying with commercial disclosure regulations and audience trust standards.
Develop high-converting brand partnership assets: sponsor pitch decks, media kits with audience demographic insights, tiered deliverables, rate card pricing formulas, usage rights, and contracts.
what_you_will_learn: How YouTube's monetization review team audits channels for advertiser-friendliness and original value
Current vs February 1, 2027 YPP threshold divergence for new applicant channels
Why existing YPP participants are not automatically subjected to retroactive entry thresholds
Distinguishing public view counts from qualified/engaged Shorts views in YPP eligibility
The Shorts Creator Pool allocation formula and music licensing deduction mechanics
Calculating effective RPM across content niches (Finance/B2B $15–$30+ vs Entertainment $2–$4)
Creator cost accounting: factoring cameras, lights, software, editors, and personal hourly wage
Designing a 2-page professional Sponsorship Media Kit in Canva with verified audience statistics
Drafting brand sponsorship proposals: deliverables (integrated shoutout vs dedicated video), revisions, and usage rights
Setting up a Sponsor CRM pipeline in Notion to track brand inquiries from lead to paid invoice
Operating an ethical creator business: zero revenue fabrication, tax compliance, and avoiding brand conflicts
key_concepts: Fan-Funding Tier vs Full Ad-Revenue Tier
Cost Per Mille (CPM) vs Revenue Per Mille (RPM)
Shorts Creator Pool Allocation & Music Deductions

Topic 02: February 1, 2027 YPP Policy Thresholds & Qualified Metrics Analysis
Topic 03: The 12 YouTube Revenue Streams: Platform Ads, Fan-Funding & Commerce
Topic 04: Creator Macroeconomics: CPM, RPM, Production Overhead & Net Margins
Topic 05: Affiliate Marketing & YouTube Shopping Architecture
Topic 06: Brand Partnerships: Media Kits, Rate Cards, Proposals & Contracting
Topic 07: Creator Business Operations: Sponsor CRM, Invoicing & Financial Health
detailed_subtopics: Topic 01: YouTube Partner Program — YPP eligibility criteria; creator account requirements; monetization policy compliance; qualified watch hours vs raw video hours; qualified Shorts views vs feed scrolls; fan-funding eligibility (lower tier) vs Ad/Premium eligibility (full tier); navigating YouTube Studio Earn tab; application workflow; human channel review process; AdSense for YouTube linkage; rejection causes (reused content, repetitive content); appeals procedure; ongoing compliance rules.

Topic 02: February 2027 YPP Changes — Official policy analysis (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12843009); February 1, 2027 entry threshold increases for new creators entering ads/Premium: 1,000 subscribers, 8,000 qualified public watch hours in 365 days OR 20M qualified Shorts views in 90 days; understanding grandfathering (existing YPP creators not automatically subject to new entry thresholds); lower-threshold fan-funding/Shopping access: 500 subscribers, 3 qualifying public uploads in 90 days, 3,000 watch hours OR 3M Shorts views; Shorts Creator Pool requirements and music deductions; channel activity maintenance rules; Premium and Premium Lite revenue shares; treating policies as time-sensitive published rules; distinguishing public views from qualified views; strict prohibition on promising YPP approval.

Topic 03: Revenue Models — Watch-page advertisements (skippable, non-skippable, bumper); YouTube Premium watch-time royalties; Shorts ad revenue sharing; Channel Memberships (perks, badges, tiers); Super Chat, Super Stickers, and Super Thanks in live streams and VODs; YouTube Shopping store integration; affiliate marketing networks (Amazon Associates, impact.com); direct brand sponsorships; digital merchandise and digital courses; creator service offerings (editing, consulting, production).

Topic 04: Creator Economics — Understanding CPM (advertiser cost per 1,000 impressions) vs RPM (creator earnings per 1,000 views after YouTube's 45% or 55% cut); revenue variability across seasons (Q4 peak vs Q1 trough); calculating revenue per video; production cost accounting (hardware depreciation, editing software, sound libraries, studio space); accounting for creator hours; gross revenue vs net operating income; break-even financial forecasting.

Topic 05: Affiliate and Shopping — Selecting products relevant to audience persona; placing affiliate links in descriptions, pinned comments, and community posts; YouTube Shopping product tagging where eligible; FTC and ASCI affiliate disclosure requirements; maintaining audience trust; avoiding predatory affiliate offers.

Topic 06: Brand Partnerships — Evaluating sponsor suitability and alignment; building a 2-page Media Kit (audience demographics, average views, engagement rate, past collaborations); brand research and cold outreach strategy; authoring sponsorship proposals; deliverable scopes (30–60s integrated shoutout, dedicated review, Shorts package); creative brief management; negotiating usage rights (organic vs paid whitelist ads), exclusivity windows, and revision limits; payment milestones (50% upfront / 50% on live URL); post-campaign performance reporting.

Topic 07: Creator Business Operations — Managing a sponsor CRM pipeline in Notion; standard contract templates; invoicing fundamentals and GST/tax registration awareness; creator bookkeeping and business bank accounts; offering freelance channel management services to external clients; hiring and collaborating with thumbnail designers and assistant editors.

learning_objectives: Implement responsible AI workflows across research, ideation, visual asset generation, and editing, ensuring distinct human creative expression and fact-checked claims.

Apply YouTube's official Altered and Synthetic Content policy (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491), accurately distinguishing between realistic synthetic media requiring upload disclosure vs standard AI productivity tools that do not.
Navigate YouTube copyright architecture: Content ID claims, copyright strikes, Fair Use/Fair Dealing boundaries, public domain assets, and commercial stock licensing registers.
Enforce advertising disclosure compliance: YouTube's 'Paid Promotion' checkbox, FTC requirements, and ASCI Influencer Guidelines for Indian creator content.
Establish creator community moderation policies to filter abusive comments, protect brand reputation, and build constructive subscriber communities.
Design robust creator production operations: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), digital asset organization, 3-2-1 backup systems, and account security protocols.
what_you_will_learn: How to use generative AI as an intellectual collaborator while maintaining authentic creator voice
Official YouTube Altered/Synthetic Content policy rules and upload checkbox requirements
What requires AI disclosure: realistic simulated human likenesses, synthetic voice cloning, manipulated real events
What does NOT require AI disclosure: AI noise reduction, color grading, script outlines, fantasy animations, or b-roll enhancement
Deconstructing Content ID: how automated audio/video fingerprints trigger claims vs copyright strikes
Copyright Strike resolution: counter-notifications, retraction requests, and copyright school
Maintaining a commercial Licensing Register for all background music, sound effects, fonts, and stock clips
Sponsorship disclosure: activating 'Paid Promotion' badges and placing clear verbal/visual notices per ASCI standards
Community management: automated blocklists, held-for-review comment filters, and de-escalation tactics

Topic 02: YouTube Synthetic & Altered Content Disclosure Policy Compliance

detailed_subtopics: Topic 01: Responsible AI Production — AI-assisted research and prompt validation; script development assistance vs lazy regurgitation; generative visual assets (Midjourney, Firefly); AI-supported video editing; AI voice generation and speech-to-speech tools; automatic dubbing workflows; fact-checking every AI-generated claim; ensuring human creative primacy; content rights management.

Topic 02: Synthetic-Content Disclosure — Official YouTube reference (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491); identifying realistic altered content; AI-generated people and synthetic faces; synthetic voices and audio clones; digital manipulation of real-world events; realistic generated scenes; upload-time disclosure settings in YouTube Studio; viewer transparency labels; distinguishing prohibited deceptive synthetic media from permitted creative generation; maintaining content provenance.

Topic 03: Copyright — Fundamentals of video and audio copyright; licensed stock media (Artlist, Storyblocks); sound effect licensing; commercial music rights; YouTube Audio Library usage; Content ID fingerprinting; Content ID claims (ad revenue redirection) vs Copyright Strikes (takedowns); 3-strike channel termination policy; reused content vs transformative value add; inauthentic content penalties; source attribution; Fair Use and Fair Dealing legal limitations.

Topic 04: Sponsorship Compliance — Paid-promotion upload disclosure checkbox; in-video sponsorship disclosure; ASCI (Advertising Standards Council of India) influencer guidelines; FTC endorsement compliance; substantiating brand claims; honest product reviews; disclosing conflicts of interest; prohibited and restricted advertising categories; brand safety standards; preserving audience trust.

Topic 05: Community Management — YouTube Studio comment moderation suite; held-for-review filters and automated blocked words; responding professionally to critical feedback; managing trolls and defusing harassment; reporting community guideline violations; fostering a loyal, civil subscriber community; reputation preservation.

Topic 06: Production Operations — Designing modular creator SOPs; multi-stage editorial review checklists; client/internal content approvals; fact-checking workflows; maintaining a Licensing Register (.xlsx); folder taxonomies and metadata tagging; 3-2-1 backup protocol (3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite/cloud); scheduled publishing; role-based channel permissions (Manager vs Editor vs Subtitle Editor); account security hardening (FIDO2 keys, anti-phishing hygiene).

Topic 07: Sustainability — Calibrating sustainable publishing capacity; production time and financial budgeting; task delegation and assistant outsourcing; avoiding creator overwork and algorithmic exhaustion; quality over volume philosophy; ethical, durable audience growth.

detailed_subtopics: Topic 01: Final Niche Review — Channel positioning stress-test; evaluating audience demand signals; validating unique value proposition (UVP) against current market saturation; confirming domain authority direction.
Topic 02: Audience & Pillars — Persona validation; reviewing content-pillar balance (Help, Hub, Hero); verifying 30-idea backlog and ensuring content diversity.

Topic 03: Long-Form Review — Forensic quality check on 3 original long-form master videos (including Month 2/3 production + 2 additional distinct productions); verifying audio levels (-14 LUFS), pacing, B-roll rhythm, and color grading consistency.
Topic 04: Shorts Review — Audit of 8 completed vertical Shorts; testing 1-second hooks, safe-zone clearance, caption animations, and seamless loop seam transitions; confirming related-video linkages.
Topic 05: Packaging Review — Reviewing 3 thumbnail concepts per video in Photoshop; mobile 120x90px legibility testing; evaluating 3 title variations per video for curiosity and clarity.
Topic 06: Publishing QA — Finalizing YouTube Studio upload checklists; verifying semantic descriptions, timestamp chapters, info card timings, end screens, and thematic playlists.
Topic 07: Analytics Validation — Evaluating channel analytics dashboard or approved anonymized training dataset; annotating retention curves to prove diagnostic ability.
Topic 08: Experimentation — Reviewing documented 'Test & Compare' A/B test logs or approved simulation experiment protocols; analyzing watch time share metrics.
Topic 09: Monetization Review — Evaluating current and February 1, 2027 YPP threshold readiness; reviewing diversified revenue roadmap (ads, fan-funding, affiliate, sponsorships).
Topic 10: Sponsorship Presentation — Pitching the completed 2-page Media Kit and tiered brand sponsorship proposal; defending rate card pricing logic.
Topic 11: Rights & Disclosures — Verifying complete Asset Licensing Register; confirming Altered/Synthetic Content disclosures for any generative assets; ASCI compliance statement.
Topic 12: Production SOP — Reviewing the creator pre-flight production checklist and file management protocols.
Topic 13: 90-Day Roadmap — Establishing a 90-day publishing calendar with process-based milestones and realistic capacity pacing.
Topic 14: Capstone Compilation — Organizing all 15 portfolio evidence categories into a unified, professional digital dossier.
Topic 15: Mock Pitch — Simulating a client pitch or agency interview, receiving constructive peer and instructor feedback.
Topic 16: Final Defense — Formal student portfolio presentation defending strategic, creative, analytical, and business decisions before the academic review board.

platform_limitations: Ask Studio availability is account-restricted and rolling out progressively; Google terms prohibit under-18 accounts from accessing generative AI features inside YouTube Studio.

YouTube's native 'Test & Compare' thumbnail A/B testing is currently available exclusively on desktop for long-form videos with Advanced Features enabled; it is not supported on YouTube Shorts, active Premieres, or Made for Kids videos.

Meaningful A/B experiment conclusions and retention diagnostics require real viewer impressions; authorized institutional sample datasets are provided for simulation where live channel traffic is insufficient.

Monetization features (AdSense, Channel Memberships, Super Features, Shopping) are subject to platform eligibility thresholds, geographic availability, and AdSense age rules (creators under 18 require an adult/guardian-managed AdSense account).
